sources.source_quote:
\fn PipelineHandler::stopDevice()
 * \brief Stop capturing from all running streams
 * \param[in] camera The camera to stop
 *
 * This function stops capturing and processing requests immediately. All
 * pending requests are cancelled and complete immediately in an error state.
 */

findings.claim_quote: PipelineHandler::stop() first calls waitingRequests.swap(data->waitingRequests_) and then calls stopDevice(camera). PipelineHandler::stop() moves all waiting requests aside so that they are not requeued when completeRequest() is called inside stopDevice(). Implementers of stopDevice() must immediately stop capturing and request processing for all running streams, and must cancel all incomplete requests for that device, completing them immediately in an error state.

findings.condition: stopDevice가 반환된 뒤 분리된 대기 요청을 처리하는 공통 정지 경로입니다.
findings.actor: PipelineHandler::stop과 doQueueRequest가 해당 카메라의 요청을 처리합니다.
findings.timing: 장치 정지 호출 뒤 취소와 순번 등록 및 완료를 수행하고 두 ASSERT 뒤 순번을 초기화합니다.
findings.scope: 공통 정지 구현의 대기 요청 처리와 큐 검사입니다.
findings.reason: 반복문의 취소와 doQueueRequest 전달, 임시 큐 등록, 두 ASSERT 및 순번 초기화가 소스와 일치합니다.
findings.claim_quote: PipelineHandler::stop()은 stopDevice()를 호출한 뒤 대기 요청을 차례로 취소하고 doQueueRequest()에 전달하며, 이 경로에서 요청에 순번을 부여하고 completeRequest()에서 완료할 수 있도록 queuedRequests_에 일시적으로 추가합니다. PipelineHandler::stop()은 대기 요청을 처리한 뒤 두 ASSERT로 queuedRequests_와 waitingRequests_가 비어 있는지 확인하고 requestSequence_에 0을 저장합니다.

findings.condition: 공통 stop이 분리한 대기 요청을 처리하는 경로
findings.actor: PipelineHandler::stop과 doQueueRequest
findings.timing: stopDevice 반환 후 대기 요청을 처리하고 최종 검사 및 초기화를 수행함
findings.scope: 대기 요청의 취소·완료 경로와 큐 검사
findings.reason: 대기 요청을 순서대로 취소해 전달하며 순번 부여와 임시 큐 등록 후 완료하는 설명이 소스 및 비교 문서와 일치한다. 앞선 큐 분리의 생략은 다른 동작을 주장하지 않는다.
findings.claim_quote: PipelineHandler::stop() calls stopDevice(), then cancels the waiting requests in order and passes each one to doQueueRequest(). On this path, requests are given a sequence number and temporarily added to queuedRequests_ so that they can be completed in completeRequest(). After processing the waiting requests, PipelineHandler::stop() checks with two ASSERT statements that queuedRequests_ and waitingRequests_ are empty, and stores 0 in requestSequence_.

findings.condition: 일반적인 획득·구성·시작과 실행 중인 카메라의 정상 정지 경로
findings.actor: 애플리케이션과 Camera
findings.timing: acquire, configure, start 후 stop을 거쳐 release
findings.scope: 카메라 상태 전이와 재시작·재구성 가능성
findings.reason: 상태도와 운영 설명이 해당 순서 및 반복 가능성을 뒷받침한다. 연결 해제 후의 별도 경로를 이 정상 종료 경로에 대한 반례로 확대하지 않는다.
findings.claim_quote: 캡처를 준비하려면 애플리케이션은 acquire()로 카메라를 획득한 뒤 configure()로 구성하고, 그다음 start()로 시작하는 순서로 진행해야 합니다. 시작된 카메라는 정지되기 전까지 요청을 처리할 수 있으며, 이 구간이 Running 상태입니다. 완전히 끝내는 경로는 Running에서 stop()으로 Stopping을 거쳐 정지 후 Configured로 돌아가고, 이어서 Configured에서 release()로 Available로 해제하는 순서입니다. 카메라가 해제되지 않은 동안에는 애플리케이션이 시작과 정지를 여러 번 반복할 수 있으며, 카메라를 재구성하여 캡처 설정을 바꿀 수도 있습니다.

findings.condition: 일반적인 획득·구성·시작과 실행 중인 카메라의 정상 정지 경로
findings.actor: 애플리케이션과 Camera
findings.timing: acquire, configure, start 후 stop을 거쳐 release
findings.scope: 카메라 상태 전이와 재시작·재구성 가능성
findings.reason: 영문은 한국어 주장과 같은 상태 전이와 가능성을 보존하며 소스의 운영 설명 및 상태도와 일치한다.
findings.claim_quote: To prepare capture, the application must acquire the camera with acquire(), configure it with configure(), and then start it with start(). A started camera can process requests until it is stopped, and this period is the Running state. The full end path runs from Running via stop() through Stopping, returns to Configured after stopping, and then goes from Configured via release() to Available, releasing the camera. While the camera is not released, the application may repeat starting and stopping multiple times, and may also change the capture settings by reconfiguring the camera.

findings.condition: PipelineHandler::stop이 호출된 경우
findings.actor: PipelineHandler::stop
findings.timing: 대기 큐 분리 직후 stopDevice 호출, 반환 후 대기 요청 처리
findings.scope: 카메라별 대기 요청의 분리와 취소 순서
findings.reason: 재큐 방지 목적, 지역 큐 교환 및 반환 후 선두부터 취소해 doQueueRequest에 전달하는 순서가 소스와 일치한다.
findings.claim_quote: PipelineHandler::stop은 카메라의 waitingRequests_를 로컬 큐와 교환해 대기 요청을 분리합니다. 이는 stopDevice() 내부에서 completeRequest()가 호출될 때 대기 요청이 다시 큐에 들어가지 않도록 하기 위한 것입니다. 분리 직후 장치 정지 함수인 stopDevice(camera)를 호출합니다. stopDevice가 반환하면 분리해 둔 대기 요청을 앞에서부터 하나씩 꺼내 취소로 표시한 뒤 doQueueRequest로 처리합니다.

findings.condition: PipelineHandler::stop이 호출된 경우
findings.actor: PipelineHandler::stop
findings.timing: 대기 큐 분리 직후 stopDevice 호출, 반환 후 대기 요청 처리
findings.scope: 카메라별 대기 요청의 분리와 취소 순서
findings.reason: 영문은 한국어 주장의 목적, 대상 및 호출 순서를 보존하며 소스 구현과 일치한다.
findings.claim_quote: PipelineHandler::stop separates the waiting requests by swapping the camera's waitingRequests_ with a local queue. This prevents the waiting requests from being requeued when completeRequest() is called inside stopDevice(). Immediately after separating them, it calls stopDevice(camera), the device stop function. When stopDevice returns, it removes the separated waiting requests one at a time from the front, marks them as cancelled, and then processes them with doQueueRequest.

findings.condition: stopDevice의 문서 계약과 공통 stop의 대기 요청 처리 경로
findings.actor: stopDevice 구현자와 PipelineHandler::stop
findings.timing: 장치 정지 중 제출된 미완료 요청을 처리하고, 반환 후 분리된 대기 요청을 처리함
findings.scope: 구현자 계약 및 공통 stop의 ASSERT와 순번 초기화
findings.reason: 장치 정지 계약과 공통 함수의 역할 구분이 소스와 일치한다. 이는 구현이 모든 장치 오류 상황에서 계약을 충족했다는 실측 보장은 아니다.

sources.source_quote:
\fn PipelineHandler::stopDevice()
 * \brief Stop capturing from all running streams
 * \param[in] camera The camera to stop
 *
 * This function stops capturing and processing requests immediately. All
 * pending requests are cancelled and complete immediately in an error state.
 */

findings.claim_quote: stopDevice 구현자는 실행 중인 모든 스트림의 캡처와 요청 처리를 즉시 중단하고, 이미 장치에 제출된 미완료 요청을 취소해 오류 상태로 즉시 완료해야 합니다. stop이 먼저 분리한 waitingRequests_의 대기 요청은 stopDevice가 반환된 뒤 stop이 취소하고 완료 처리합니다. stop의 마지막에서 ASSERT는 queuedRequests_와 waitingRequests_가 각각 비어 있는지 확인합니다. 이어서 요청 순번 requestSequence_를 0으로 초기화합니다.

findings.condition: Stopping with requests already submitted to the device and requests still waiting in the common queue.
findings.actor: The device-specific stopDevice implementer handles device requests; PipelineHandler::stop handles the detached waiting requests.
findings.timing: The common stop detaches waiting requests before stopDevice, handles them after it returns, then checks both queues and resets the sequence.
findings.scope: The stopDevice statement is a documented contract; the UVC failure path does not establish that every implementation satisfies it.
findings.reason: The source separates the device stop contract from the common handler's waiting-request cancellation. The sequence reset and assertions match the implementation; the peers' UVC failure discussion concerns verification of implementation behavior, not a different contract.
findings.claim_quote: The stopDevice implementer must immediately stop capture from all running streams and request processing, cancel incomplete requests already submitted to the device, and immediately complete them in an error state. After stopDevice returns, stop cancels and completes the waiting requests from waitingRequests_ that stop separated beforehand. At the end of stop, ASSERT checks that queuedRequests_ and waitingRequests_ are each empty. The request sequence number requestSequence_ is then reset to 0.

findings.condition: Normal completion dispatches eligible waiting requests; during stop the original waiting queue has been detached.
findings.actor: PipelineHandler::completeRequest, doQueueRequests and stop.
findings.timing: Completion calls doQueueRequests at the end; stop detaches the waiting queue before calling stopDevice.
findings.scope: The non-resubmission statement concerns the original detached waiting requests during reentry.
findings.reason: The source has the stated capacity and prepared-state breaks, removes the head before dispatch, and swaps out the waiting queue to prevent its requeue during stopDevice completion. The English claim and relevant peers preserve those conditions.
findings.claim_quote: 정상 완료 시 completeRequest는 끝에서 doQueueRequests를 호출하며, waitingRequests_가 비어 있지 않은 동안 queuedRequests_.size() == maxQueuedRequestsDevice_이면 반복을 중단하고, 선두 요청의 prepared_가 거짓이어도 중단하며, 두 중단 조건에 해당하지 않으면 선두 요청을 큐에서 꺼내 전달합니다. 정지 시 stop은 waitingRequests_를 먼저 분리하므로 stopDevice 안에서 완료 처리가 재진입해도 원래 대기 요청을 다시 제출하지 않습니다.

findings.condition: Normal completion dispatches eligible waiting requests; during stop the original waiting queue has been detached.
findings.actor: PipelineHandler::completeRequest, doQueueRequests and stop.
findings.timing: Completion calls doQueueRequests at the end; stop detaches the waiting queue before calling stopDevice.
findings.scope: The non-resubmission statement concerns the original detached waiting requests during reentry.
findings.reason: The translation retains the source's exact capacity test, unprepared-head condition and stop-specific queue separation. The cited peers describe the same processing and cancellation paths.
findings.claim_quote: On normal completion, completeRequest calls doQueueRequests at the end. While waitingRequests_ is not empty, doQueueRequests stops the loop if queuedRequests_.size() == maxQueuedRequestsDevice_, and also stops if the first request's prepared_ is false. If neither stopping condition applies, doQueueRequests removes the first request from the queue and passes it on. When stopping, stop first detaches waitingRequests_, so the original waiting requests are not resubmitted even if completion processing is reentered inside stopDevice.

findings.condition: A registered request enters preparation; preparation failure causes cancellation.
findings.actor: PipelineHandler registers and queues the request; Request::Private performs preparation.
findings.timing: The request is added to the waiting queue before prepare is called; the prepared signal triggers dispatch.
findings.scope: Source contract and implementation of request preparation, including failed preparation.
findings.reason: The source supports the signal connection, 300 ms prepare argument and cancellation on preparation failure. The peers provide further detail without changing those claims.
findings.claim_quote: PipelineHandler::registerRequest()는 요청이 준비되면 doQueueRequests(request->_d()->camera())를 호출하도록 prepared 신호를 연결합니다. PipelineHandler::queueRequest()는 요청을 waitingRequests_에 추가한 뒤 prepare(300ms)를 호출합니다. 요청이 준비 단계에서 실패하면 취소됩니다.

findings.condition: A registered request enters preparation; preparation failure causes cancellation.
findings.actor: PipelineHandler registers and queues the request; Request::Private performs preparation.
findings.timing: The request is added to the waiting queue before prepare is called; the prepared signal triggers dispatch.
findings.scope: Source contract and implementation of request preparation, including failed preparation.
findings.reason: The translation preserves the signal connection, call order, timeout argument and cancellation condition supported by the source and Korean peer.
findings.claim_quote: PipelineHandler::registerRequest() connects the prepared signal so that doQueueRequests(request->_d()->camera()) is called when the request is ready. PipelineHandler::queueRequest() adds the request to waitingRequests_ and then calls prepare(300ms). If the request fails during preparation, it is cancelled.

findings.condition: The branch depends on whether the request is already cancelled and, otherwise, on the device submission result.
findings.actor: PipelineHandler::doQueueRequest.
findings.timing: Queue insertion and sequence assignment precede the cancellation test; device submission occurs only on the other branch.
findings.scope: The named function's handling of one request, including requests cancelled before dispatch.
findings.reason: The source performs the stated sequence increment, completes and returns for an already cancelled request, and calls cancelRequest on a nonzero device result. The shortened member references identify the same request and camera-private objects in this function.
findings.claim_quote: doQueueRequest는 요청을 queuedRequests_에 추가하고 sequence_에 requestSequence_ 값을 할당한 뒤 requestSequence_를 증가시킵니다. cancelled_가 참이면 completeRequest를 호출하고 함수를 종료합니다. 그렇지 않으면 queueRequestDevice를 호출하며, 그 결과가 0이 아니면 cancelRequest를 호출합니다.

findings.condition: Already-cancelled requests take the completion branch; other requests are submitted to the device and cancelled on a nonzero result.
findings.actor: PipelineHandler::doQueueRequest.
findings.timing: Queue registration and sequence assignment precede the conditional branches.
findings.scope: Common request dispatch, including requests marked cancelled during stop.
findings.reason: The source supports both branches and the sequence operation. The Korean peer agrees; the stop peer describes a compatible way to enter the cancelled branch.
findings.claim_quote: doQueueRequest adds the request to queuedRequests_, assigns the value of requestSequence_ to sequence_, and then increments requestSequence_. If cancelled_ is true, doQueueRequest calls completeRequest and exits. Otherwise, doQueueRequest calls queueRequestDevice and, if queueRequestDevice returns a nonzero result, calls cancelRequest.

findings.condition: Preparation completes synchronously without fences, or after fence notification or timeout; dispatch is limited by queue capacity and head readiness.
findings.actor: PipelineHandler and Request::Private; an investigator observes the specified boundaries.
findings.timing: The prepared flag is set before the signal, including after timeout cancellation.
findings.scope: Request preparation and a proposed missing-completion investigation.
findings.reason: The source supports the queue and preparation branches, including cancellation before the prepared signal. The observation is a plan, not an executed result; the English and manuscript peers agree.
findings.claim_quote: PipelineHandler::queueRequest()는 요청을 waitingRequests_에 넣고 prepare(300ms)를 호출하며, doQueueRequests()는 큐가 가득 찼거나 선두 요청의 prepared_가 거짓이면 순회를 멈춥니다. Request::Private::prepare()는 fence가 없으면 동기적으로 준비 완료를 알리고, fence가 있으면 notifiers_로 기다리며, notifierActivated()가 마지막 fence를 처리하거나 timeout()이 요청을 취소하면 emitPrepareCompleted()가 prepared_를 참으로 바꾼 뒤 prepared 신호를 보냅니다. 따라서 prepared_는 촬영 준비 성공을 뜻하지 않으며, 완료 누락 조사에서는 waitingRequests_ 선두의 prepared_, notifiers_에 남은 fence, notifierActivated()와 timeout()의 실행 및 다음 분기를 관찰합니다.

findings.condition: Preparation completes synchronously without fences, or after fence notification or timeout; dispatch is limited by queue capacity and head readiness.
findings.actor: PipelineHandler and Request::Private; an investigator observes the specified boundaries.
findings.timing: The prepared flag is set before the signal, including after timeout cancellation.
findings.scope: Request preparation and a proposed missing-completion investigation.
findings.reason: The translation preserves the source-backed branches and the distinction between preparation completion and successful capture preparation. Its observation is a plan and agrees with the Korean peers.
findings.claim_quote: PipelineHandler::queueRequest() puts the request in waitingRequests_ and calls prepare(300ms), while doQueueRequests() stops iterating if the queue is full or the leading request's prepared_ is false. Request::Private::prepare() synchronously signals preparation completion if there are no fences and waits using notifiers_ if there are fences. When notifierActivated() handles the last fence or timeout() cancels the request, emitPrepareCompleted() sets prepared_ to true and then emits the prepared signal. Therefore, prepared_ does not mean preparation for capture succeeded. In an investigation of missing completions, observe prepared_ at the head of waitingRequests_, fences remaining in notifiers_, the execution of notifierActivated() and timeout(), and the subsequent branches.

findings.condition: Dispatch stops at the device queue limit or an unprepared head; cancellation or device submission failure can reach completion processing.
findings.actor: PipelineHandler::doQueueRequests and its completion path; an investigator observes possible duplicate processing.
findings.timing: The ready head is removed before doQueueRequest; completeRequest subsequently calls doQueueRequests.
findings.scope: Waiting-queue dispatch and a proposed investigation of reentrancy.
findings.reason: The code and its comment support the removal order and recursion rationale. The completion path supports the stated possibility; the English and manuscript peers agree, and the investigation does not assert a measured result.
findings.claim_quote: doQueueRequests()는 queuedRequests_.size() == maxQueuedRequestsDevice_이거나 대기 큐의 선두 요청이 준비되지 않았으면 반복을 중단하고, 준비된 선두 요청은 큐에서 제거한 뒤 doQueueRequest()를 호출합니다. 이 제거 순서는 doQueueRequest() 안에서 doQueueRequests()가 재귀 호출되는 경우를 고려한 것이며, 준비 중 취소된 요청이나 장치 제출에 실패한 요청은 완료 처리를 거쳐 다시 doQueueRequests()를 호출할 수 있습니다. 조사 계획으로는 이 제거 순서를 변경하기 전에 대기 큐의 선두와 제거 순서, 각 요청의 중복 처리 여부를 관찰합니다.

findings.condition: Dispatch stops at the device queue limit or an unprepared head; cancellation or device submission failure can reach completion processing.
findings.actor: PipelineHandler::doQueueRequests and its completion path; an investigator observes possible duplicate processing.
findings.timing: The ready head is removed before doQueueRequest; completeRequest subsequently calls doQueueRequests.
findings.scope: Waiting-queue dispatch and a proposed investigation of reentrancy.
findings.reason: The translation preserves the conditions, ordering and possibility of recursion. The source supports these details, and the Korean peers describe the same plan without claiming it was executed.
findings.claim_quote: doQueueRequests() stops iterating if queuedRequests_.size() == maxQueuedRequestsDevice_ or if the request at the head of the waiting queue is not ready; it removes a ready head request from the queue before calling doQueueRequest(). This removal order accounts for recursive calls to doQueueRequests() from within doQueueRequest(), and requests cancelled during preparation or whose submission to the device failed may lead to another call to doQueueRequests() through completion processing. The investigation plan is to observe the head of the waiting queue, the removal order, and whether each request is processed more than once before changing this removal order.

findings.condition: The caller must synchronize stop with other camera-state-changing functions; the order of a posted queue call relative to stop is an investigation question.
findings.actor: Camera caller, Camera::queueRequest, PipelineHandler::queueRequest and investigator.
findings.timing: The camera state can change after the access check; the plan records posting, execution, stop and completion boundaries.
findings.scope: Source-level synchronization obligation and an unexecuted ordering investigation, not a claim that a late execution occurred.
findings.reason: The sources support the caller obligation, queued invocation, queue implementation and stop sequence. The English and manuscript peers preserve the conditional investigation rather than asserting a runtime outcome.
findings.claim_quote: 호출자는 이미 제출된 요청이 있는 경우에도 Camera::stop()을 다른 카메라 상태 변경 함수와 동기화해야 합니다. Camera::queueRequest()는 상태 검사 후에도 함수 실행 중 카메라 상태가 바뀔 수 있다고 명시하며, 게시된 PipelineHandler::queueRequest()는 CameraStopping을 재검사하지 않고 요청을 waitingRequests_에 추가한 뒤 prepare(300ms)를 실행합니다. 조사 계획으로, 게시된 호출이 정지 시 대기 큐를 분리한 뒤 실행되는지 확인하기 위해 호출 게시와 실행, CameraStopping 설정, 대기 큐 분리, stopDevice(), 준비, 장치 제출 및 Camera::requestComplete() 상태 검사의 순서를 기록합니다.

sources.source_quote:
\brief Create a request object for the camera
 * \param[in] cookie Opaque cookie for application use
 *
 * This function creates an empty request for the application to fill with
 * buffers and parameters, and queue for capture.
 *
 * The \a cookie is stored in the request and is accessible through the
 * Request::cookie() function at any time. It is typically used by applications
 * to map the request to an external resource in the request completion
 * handler, and is completely opaque to libcamera.
 *
 * The ownership of the returned request is passed to the caller, which is
 * responsible for deleting it. The request may be deleted in the completion
 * handler, or reused after resetting its state with Request::reuse().
 *
 * \context This function is \threadsafe. It may only be called when the camera
 * is in the Configured or Running state as defined in \ref camera_operation.
 *
 * \return A pointer to the newly created request, or nullptr on error
 */
std::unique_ptr<Request> Camera::createRequest(uint64_t cookie)

\brief Add a FrameBuffer with its associated Stream to the Request
 * \param[in] stream The stream the buffer belongs to
 * \param[in] buffer The FrameBuffer to add to the request
 * \param[in] fence The optional fence
 *
 * A reference to the buffer is stored in the request. The caller is responsible
 * for ensuring that the buffer will remain valid until the request complete
 * callback is called.
 *
 * A request can only contain one buffer per stream. If a buffer has already
 * been added to the request for the same stream, this function returns -EEXIST.
 *
 * A Fence can be optionally associated with the \a buffer.
 *
 * When a valid Fence is provided to this function, \a fence is moved to \a
 * buffer and this Request will only be queued to the device once the
 * fences of all its buffers have been correctly signalled. Ownership of the
 * fence will only be taken in case of success, otherwise the fence will
 * be left unmodified.
 *
 * If the \a fence associated with \a buffer isn't signalled, the request will
 * fail after a timeout. The buffer will still contain the fence, which
 * applications must retrieve with FrameBuffer::releaseFence() before the buffer
 * can be reused in another request. Attempting to add a buffer that still
 * contains a fence to a request will result in this function returning -EEXIST.
 *
 * \sa FrameBuffer::releaseFence()
 *
 * \return 0 on success or a negative error code otherwise
 * \retval -EEXIST The request already contains a buffer for the stream
 *  or the buffer still references a fence
 * \retval -EINVAL The buffer does not reference a valid Stream
 */
int Request::addBuffer(const Stream *stream, FrameBuffer *buffer,

findings.claim_quote: Camera::createRequest() 호출자는 반환된 Request의 소유권을 받으며 삭제할 책임이 있습니다. 호출자는 완료 핸들러에서 요청을 삭제하거나 Request::reuse()로 상태를 초기화한 뒤 재사용할 수 있습니다. Request::addBuffer()는 버퍼 참조를 요청에 저장하며, 호출자는 요청 완료 콜백이 호출될 때까지 버퍼가 유효하도록 해야 합니다. 파이프라인 핸들러는 completeRequest() 또는 cancelRequest()가 반환된 뒤 해당 요청에 접근해서는 안 됩니다.

findings.claim_quote: Separate from the preceding normal completion example, this is a case where the pipeline handler calls cancelRequest(B) instead of completeRequest(B) when both request A at the front of the submission queue and request B are RequestPending. Request::Private::doCancelRequest cancels each of B's pending_ buffers and emits bufferCompleted, then sets cancelled_ to true and clears pending_. cancelRequest calls completeRequest after cancel, and Request::Private::complete selects RequestCancelled as B's status. If A at the front is still RequestPending, B's return to the application is delayed, and the common rules described earlier apply to buffer lifetime and the handler's access to the request.

\brief Add a FrameBuffer with its associated Stream to the Request
 * \param[in] stream The stream the buffer belongs to
 * \param[in] buffer The FrameBuffer to add to the request
 * \param[in] fence The optional fence
 *
 * A reference to the buffer is stored in the request. The caller is responsible
 * for ensuring that the buffer will remain valid until the request complete
 * callback is called.
 *
 * A request can only contain one buffer per stream. If a buffer has already
 * been added to the request for the same stream, this function returns -EEXIST.
 *
 * A Fence can be optionally associated with the \a buffer.
 *
 * When a valid Fence is provided to this function, \a fence is moved to \a
 * buffer and this Request will only be queued to the device once the
 * fences of all its buffers have been correctly signalled. Ownership of the
 * fence will only be taken in case of success, otherwise the fence will
 * be left unmodified.
 *
 * If the \a fence associated with \a buffer isn't signalled, the request will
 * fail after a timeout. The buffer will still contain the fence, which
 * applications must retrieve with FrameBuffer::releaseFence() before the buffer
 * can be reused in another request. Attempting to add a buffer that still
 * contains a fence to a request will result in this function returning -EEXIST.
 *
 * \sa FrameBuffer::releaseFence()
 *
 * \return 0 on success or a negative error code otherwise
 * \retval -EEXIST The request already contains a buffer for the stream
 *  or the buffer still references a fence
 * \retval -EINVAL The buffer does not reference a valid Stream
 */
int Request::addBuffer(const Stream *stream, FrameBuffer *buffer,

findings.claim_quote: The investigation plan is to confirm that the common contract of stopDevice is to immediately stop capture from all running streams and request processing, cancel all pending requests, and complete them immediately in an error state. The plan will then identify the target device's PipelineHandler and examine the path that cancels and completes in-progress requests in the corresponding stopDevice implementation. It will separately observe and compare the point where waitingRequests_ is detached in PipelineHandler::stop, the point immediately before the stopDevice call, entry into the actual implementation, and its return. A marker immediately before the call alone does not establish that the device stopped internally, and the cause of a return not being observed within the selected observation window remains undetermined. The plan will record the request values passed to doQueueRequest(request) by the cancellation loop in PipelineHandler::stop() during the existing execution.

findings.claim_quote: PipelineHandler::stop swaps waitingRequests_ into a local queue using swap so that waiting requests are not requeued when completeRequest() is called inside stopDevice. // SPDX-License-Identifier: CC-BY-SA-4.0

/**
 * \page thread-safety Reentrancy and Thread-Safety
 *
 * Through the documentation, several terms are used to define how classes and
 * their member functions can be used from multiple threads.
 *
 * - A **reentrant** function may be called simultaneously from multiple
 *   threads if and only if each invocation uses a different instance of the
 *   class. This is the default for all member functions not explictly marked
 *   otherwise.
 *
 * - \anchor thread-safe A **thread-safe** function may be called
 *   simultaneously from multiple threads on the same instance of a class. A
 *   thread-safe function is thus reentrant. Thread-safe functions may also be
 *   called simultaneously with any other reentrant function of the same class
 *   on the same instance.
 *
 * \internal
 * - \anchor thread-bound A **thread-bound** function may be called only from
 *   the thread that the class instances lives in (see section \ref
 *   thread-objects). For instances of classes that do not derive from the
 *   Object class, this is the thread in which the instance was created. A
 *   thread-bound function is not thread-safe, and may or may not be reentrant.
 * \endinternal
 *
 * Neither reentrancy nor thread-safety, in this context, mean that a function
 * may be called simultaneously from the same thread, for instance from a
 * callback invoked by the function. This may deadlock and isn't allowed unless
 * separately documented.
 *
 * \if internal
 * A class is defined as reentrant, thread-safe or thread-bound if all its
 * member functions are reentrant, thread-safe or thread-bound respectively.
 * \else
 * A class is defined as reentrant or thread-safe if all its member functions
 * are reentrant or thread-safe respectively.
 * \endif
 * Some member functions may additionally be documented as having additional
 * thread-related attributes.
 *
 * Most classes are reentrant but not thread-safe, as making them fully
 * thread-safe would incur locking costs considered prohibitive for the
 * expected use cases.
 */

\enum FrameMetadata::Status
 * \brief Define the frame completion status
 * \var FrameMetadata::FrameSuccess
 * The frame has been captured with success and contains valid data. All fields
 * of the FrameMetadata structure are valid.
 * \var FrameMetadata::FrameError
 * The frame data is partly or fully corrupted, missing or otherwise invalid.
 * This can for instance indicate a hardware transmission error, or invalid data
 * produced by the sensor during its startup phase. The sequence and timestamp
 * fields of the FrameMetadata structure is valid, all the other fields may be
 * invalid.
 * \var FrameMetadata::FrameCancelled
 * Capture stopped before the frame completed. The frame data is not valid. All
 * fields of the FrameMetadata structure but the status field are invalid.
 * \var FrameMetadata::FrameStartup
 * The frame has been successfully captured. However, the IPA is in a
 * cold-start or reset phase and will result in image quality parameters
 * producing unusable images. Applications are recommended to not consume these
 * frames. All other fields of the FrameMetadata structure are valid.
 */

\class Signal
 * \brief Generic signal and slot communication mechanism
 *
 * Signals and slots are a language construct aimed at communication between
 * objects through the observer pattern without the need for boilerplate code.
 * See http://doc.qt.io/qt-6/signalsandslots.html for more information.
 *
 * Signals model events that can be observed from objects unrelated to the event
 * source. Slots are functions that are called in response to a signal. Signals
 * can be connected to and disconnected from slots dynamically at runtime. When
 * a signal is emitted, all connected slots are called sequentially in the order
 * they have been connected.
 *
 * Signals are defined with zero, one or more typed parameters. They are emitted
 * with a value for each of the parameters, and those values are passed to the
 * connected slots.
 *
 * Slots are normal static or class member functions. In order to be connected
 * to a signal, their signature must match the signal type (taking the same
 * arguments as the signal and returning void).
 *
 * Connecting a signal to a slot results in the slot being called with the
 * arguments passed to the emit() function when the signal is emitted. Multiple
 * slots can be connected to the same signal, and multiple signals can connected
 * to the same slot.
 *
 * When a slot belongs to an instance of the Object class, the slot is called
 * in the context of the thread that the object is bound to. If the signal is
 * emitted from the same thread, the slot will be called synchronously, before
 * Signal::emit() returns. If the signal is emitted from a different thread,
 * the slot will be called asynchronously from the object's thread's event
 * loop, after the Signal::emit() function returns, with a copy of the signal's
 * arguments. The emitter shall thus ensure that any pointer or reference
 * passed through the signal will remain valid after the signal is emitted.
 *
 * Duplicate connections between a signal and a slot are not expected and use of
 * the Object class to manage signals will enforce this restriction.
 */

\brief Add a FrameBuffer with its associated Stream to the Request
 * \param[in] stream The stream the buffer belongs to
 * \param[in] buffer The FrameBuffer to add to the request
 * \param[in] fence The optional fence
 *
 * A reference to the buffer is stored in the request. The caller is responsible
 * for ensuring that the buffer will remain valid until the request complete
 * callback is called.
 *
 * A request can only contain one buffer per stream. If a buffer has already
 * been added to the request for the same stream, this function returns -EEXIST.
 *
 * A Fence can be optionally associated with the \a buffer.
 *
 * When a valid Fence is provided to this function, \a fence is moved to \a
 * buffer and this Request will only be queued to the device once the
 * fences of all its buffers have been correctly signalled. Ownership of the
 * fence will only be taken in case of success, otherwise the fence will
 * be left unmodified.
 *
 * If the \a fence associated with \a buffer isn't signalled, the request will
 * fail after a timeout. The buffer will still contain the fence, which
 * applications must retrieve with FrameBuffer::releaseFence() before the buffer
 * can be reused in another request. Attempting to add a buffer that still
 * contains a fence to a request will result in this function returning -EEXIST.
 *
 * \sa FrameBuffer::releaseFence()
 *
 * \return 0 on success or a negative error code otherwise
 * \retval -EEXIST The request already contains a buffer for the stream
 *  or the buffer still references a fence
 * \retval -EINVAL The buffer does not reference a valid Stream
 */
int Request::addBuffer(const Stream *stream, FrameBuffer *buffer,

// SPDX-License-Identifier: CC-BY-SA-4.0

/**
 * \page thread-safety Reentrancy and Thread-Safety
 *
 * Through the documentation, several terms are used to define how classes and
 * their member functions can be used from multiple threads.
 *
 * - A **reentrant** function may be called simultaneously from multiple
 *   threads if and only if each invocation uses a different instance of the
 *   class. This is the default for all member functions not explictly marked
 *   otherwise.
 *
 * - \anchor thread-safe A **thread-safe** function may be called
 *   simultaneously from multiple threads on the same instance of a class. A
 *   thread-safe function is thus reentrant. Thread-safe functions may also be
 *   called simultaneously with any other reentrant function of the same class
 *   on the same instance.
 *
 * \internal
 * - \anchor thread-bound A **thread-bound** function may be called only from
 *   the thread that the class instances lives in (see section \ref
 *   thread-objects). For instances of classes that do not derive from the
 *   Object class, this is the thread in which the instance was created. A
 *   thread-bound function is not thread-safe, and may or may not be reentrant.
 * \endinternal
 *
 * Neither reentrancy nor thread-safety, in this context, mean that a function
 * may be called simultaneously from the same thread, for instance from a
 * callback invoked by the function. This may deadlock and isn't allowed unless
 * separately documented.
 *
 * \if internal
 * A class is defined as reentrant, thread-safe or thread-bound if all its
 * member functions are reentrant, thread-safe or thread-bound respectively.
 * \else
 * A class is defined as reentrant or thread-safe if all its member functions
 * are reentrant or thread-safe respectively.
 * \endif
 * Some member functions may additionally be documented as having additional
 * thread-related attributes.
 *
 * Most classes are reentrant but not thread-safe, as making them fully
 * thread-safe would incur locking costs considered prohibitive for the
 * expected use cases.
 */

\class Signal
 * \brief Generic signal and slot communication mechanism
 *
 * Signals and slots are a language construct aimed at communication between
 * objects through the observer pattern without the need for boilerplate code.
 * See http://doc.qt.io/qt-6/signalsandslots.html for more information.
 *
 * Signals model events that can be observed from objects unrelated to the event
 * source. Slots are functions that are called in response to a signal. Signals
 * can be connected to and disconnected from slots dynamically at runtime. When
 * a signal is emitted, all connected slots are called sequentially in the order
 * they have been connected.
 *
 * Signals are defined with zero, one or more typed parameters. They are emitted
 * with a value for each of the parameters, and those values are passed to the
 * connected slots.
 *
 * Slots are normal static or class member functions. In order to be connected
 * to a signal, their signature must match the signal type (taking the same
 * arguments as the signal and returning void).
 *
 * Connecting a signal to a slot results in the slot being called with the
 * arguments passed to the emit() function when the signal is emitted. Multiple
 * slots can be connected to the same signal, and multiple signals can connected
 * to the same slot.
 *
 * When a slot belongs to an instance of the Object class, the slot is called
 * in the context of the thread that the object is bound to. If the signal is
 * emitted from the same thread, the slot will be called synchronously, before
 * Signal::emit() returns. If the signal is emitted from a different thread,
 * the slot will be called asynchronously from the object's thread's event
 * loop, after the Signal::emit() function returns, with a copy of the signal's
 * arguments. The emitter shall thus ensure that any pointer or reference
 * passed through the signal will remain valid after the signal is emitted.
 *
 * Duplicate connections between a signal and a slot are not expected and use of
 * the Object class to manage signals will enforce this restriction.
 */

 * \fn Signal::connect

\brief Create a request object for the camera
 * \param[in] cookie Opaque cookie for application use
 *
 * This function creates an empty request for the application to fill with
 * buffers and parameters, and queue for capture.
 *
 * The \a cookie is stored in the request and is accessible through the
 * Request::cookie() function at any time. It is typically used by applications
 * to map the request to an external resource in the request completion
 * handler, and is completely opaque to libcamera.
 *
 * The ownership of the returned request is passed to the caller, which is
 * responsible for deleting it. The request may be deleted in the completion
 * handler, or reused after resetting its state with Request::reuse().
 *
 * \context This function is \threadsafe. It may only be called when the camera
 * is in the Configured or Running state as defined in \ref camera_operation.
 *
 * \return A pointer to the newly created request, or nullptr on error
 */
std::unique_ptr<Request> Camera::createRequest(uint64_t cookie)

\brief Add a FrameBuffer with its associated Stream to the Request
 * \param[in] stream The stream the buffer belongs to
 * \param[in] buffer The FrameBuffer to add to the request
 * \param[in] fence The optional fence
 *
 * A reference to the buffer is stored in the request. The caller is responsible
 * for ensuring that the buffer will remain valid until the request complete
 * callback is called.
 *
 * A request can only contain one buffer per stream. If a buffer has already
 * been added to the request for the same stream, this function returns -EEXIST.
 *
 * A Fence can be optionally associated with the \a buffer.
 *
 * When a valid Fence is provided to this function, \a fence is moved to \a
 * buffer and this Request will only be queued to the device once the
 * fences of all its buffers have been correctly signalled. Ownership of the
 * fence will only be taken in case of success, otherwise the fence will
 * be left unmodified.
 *
 * If the \a fence associated with \a buffer isn't signalled, the request will
 * fail after a timeout. The buffer will still contain the fence, which
 * applications must retrieve with FrameBuffer::releaseFence() before the buffer
 * can be reused in another request. Attempting to add a buffer that still
 * contains a fence to a request will result in this function returning -EEXIST.
 *
 * \sa FrameBuffer::releaseFence()
 *
 * \return 0 on success or a negative error code otherwise
 * \retval -EEXIST The request already contains a buffer for the stream
 *  or the buffer still references a fence
 * \retval -EINVAL The buffer does not reference a valid Stream
 */
int Request::addBuffer(const Stream *stream, FrameBuffer *buffer,

findings.claim_quote: In the unexecuted verification plan, which includes additional instrumentation, the poll ret, fd, revents, and deadline for the same processing iteration are recorded, along with the actual entry order of processNotifiers, processTimers, notifierActivated, and timeout; dispatcher timer registration and removal; the presence of the timer_ pointer; and cancelled_ and prepared_. When ret > 0, processNotifiers runs before processTimers, so the passage of the deadline alone does not establish that timeout ran first. The plan distinguishes the case where processing the last fence leads to prepared after timer_.reset from the case where another fence remains and the request is cancelled in timeout. Timer pointer presence, dispatcher registration, and actual timeout invocation are checked separately, and cancellation due to a subsequent queueRequestDevice failure is also recorded separately.

findings.claim_quote: 미실행 시험 1에서 UVC의 processControls가 0을 반환한 뒤 queueBuffer가 State::Stopping이면 cache get 전에 -ESHUTDOWN을 반환하는지 확인합니다. 정지 상태가 아니고 cache가 있어 get에 도달한 경우 free 항목이 없으면 -ENOENT, 새 예약과 scope_exit put 부재, QBUF 호출 0회를 기록합니다. 요청별로 개별 제어 변환 반환값, ControlList와 setControls 결과를 기록하며, 개별 변환 반환값은 반복문에서 전달되지 않음을 구분합니다.

findings.condition: The stopping and no-free-cache-entry cases have separate preconditions; UVC control processing has returned 0.
findings.actor: UVC queueRequestDevice, V4L2VideoDevice and the proposed test observer.
findings.timing: The stopping check precedes cache get; a failed get precedes guard construction and QBUF.
findings.scope: An unexecuted UVC test plan and the source-level control loop; no test outcome is claimed.
findings.reason: The plan preserves the relevant branches and matches its Korean counterpart. The loop ignores individual conversion return values.
findings.claim_quote: In unexecuted test 1, the plan is to check whether, after UVC's processControls returns 0, queueBuffer returns -ESHUTDOWN before the cache get when the state is State::Stopping. If the state is not stopping, a cache exists, and get is reached but there are no free entries, the plan is to record -ENOENT, the absence of a new reservation and a scope_exit put, and zero QBUF calls. For each request, the plan is to record individual control conversion return values and the results of ControlList and setControls, noting that individual conversion return values are not propagated by the loop.

findings.condition: A cache index has been obtained and either the plane count is insufficient or a count mismatch is accompanied by non-contiguity.
findings.actor: V4L2VideoDevice, the UVC and common pipeline handlers, and the proposed test observer.
findings.timing: The validation failures precede QBUF and queued-buffer registration; cancellation follows the propagated device-queue failure.
findings.scope: An unexecuted fault-injection plan, including pending-buffer notification and explicit request completion.
findings.reason: The guard releases the acquired index on either validation failure. The common handler cancels on a nonzero submission result, and cancellation handles pending buffers before request completion. The English translation agrees.
findings.claim_quote: 미실행 시험 2에서 인덱스를 얻은 뒤 플레인 수 부족과 수 불일치·비연속 조건을 각각 주입합니다. 각각 -EINVAL, 해당 인덱스의 guard put, QBUF 호출 0회와 이번 버퍼의 신규 등록 부재를 기록합니다. 요청별로 음수 반환의 전달과 cancelRequest에 따른 대기 버퍼 취소·완료 알림 및 요청 완료를 기록하며, 전체 제어 적용이나 롤백을 가정하지 않습니다.

findings.timing: The validation failures precede QBUF and queued-buffer registration; cancellation follows the propagated device-queue failure.
findings.scope: An unexecuted fault-injection plan, including pending-buffer notification and explicit request completion.
findings.reason: The English plan retains the Korean conditions and effects. The sources support the guard put, failure propagation and cancellation path without establishing an executed test.
findings.claim_quote: In unexecuted test 2, the plan is to inject insufficient plane count and mismatched plane count with non-contiguity as separate conditions after obtaining an index. For each, the plan is to record -EINVAL, the guard put for that index, zero QBUF calls, and the absence of a new registration for this buffer. For each request, the plan is to record propagation of the negative return, cancellation and completion notification of pending buffers due to cancelRequest, and request completion, without assuming that all controls were applied or rolled back.

findings.claim_quote: The public virtual CPU probe was run three times. In each run, four requests were reported as RequestComplete, four as RequestCancelled, and there were 24 callbacks. There were 72 callbacks in total. In the public Virtual2 virtual probe on Ubuntu WSL2, Auto and Queued callbacks ran on the receiving object's main thread, while Direct callbacks ran on a different thread. Markers near callback entry and return for requests cancelled during stop were observed after stop-return for Auto and Queued, and between stop-enter and stop-return for Direct. The stop-enter and stop-return markers are application markers before and after the camera->stop() call, not exact instruction boundaries inside the function.

findings.condition: Preparation considers acquire fences on pending buffers; a timer is created only when a fence requires waiting and timeout is nonzero.
findings.actor: Request::Private::prepare and its notifier and timer handlers.
findings.timing: No-fence preparation signals immediately; otherwise completion follows fence handling or timeout.
findings.scope: The supplied preparation implementation and its documented timeout contract.
findings.reason: The notifier setup, early return, conditional timer creation and stated thread-binding purpose match the source. The preparation peers describe the same completion paths.
findings.claim_quote: Request::Private::prepare는 pending_에 있는 각 FrameBuffer의 획득 펜스마다 fd를 읽기 대기하는 EventNotifier를 만들어 연결하며, 펜스가 신호되면 notifierActivated가 호출됩니다. 대기할 펜스가 없으면 notifiers_가 비어 있게 되므로 Request::prepared 신호를 즉시 발생시키고 바로 반환합니다. 선택적 timeout 인자가 0ms가 아니고 대기할 펜스가 있을 때에만 Timer를 만들어 timeout 시간으로 시작하며, 만료 시점에 모든 펜스가 올바르게 신호되지 않았다면 Request가 취소되고 Request::prepared 신호가 발생합니다. 이 타이머는 Request 생성자가 아니라 prepare 호출 시점에 만들어지는데, 파이프라인 핸들러 스레드에 바인딩되도록 하기 위해서입니다.

findings.condition: Preparation has no fences, or has fences with an optional nonzero timeout.
findings.actor: Request::Private::prepare and its notifier and timeout handlers.
findings.timing: Preparation signals immediately without fences; otherwise notification or timeout completes preparation.
findings.scope: Source implementation and thread-binding rationale, not device verification.
findings.reason: The notifier setup, empty-notifier branch, conditional timer creation and timeout cancellation agree with the sources and the related preparation claims.
findings.claim_quote: Request::Private::prepare creates and connects EventNotifier, which waits for the fd to become readable, for each acquire fence of each FrameBuffer in pending_, and notifierActivated is called when a fence is signalled. If there are no fences to wait on, notifiers_ is empty, so the Request::prepared signal is emitted immediately and the return happens right away. Only when the optional timeout argument is not 0 ms and there are fences to wait on is Timer created and started with the timeout duration; if not all fences have been correctly signalled when the timeout expires, Request is cancelled and the Request::prepared signal is emitted. This timer is created when prepare is called, not in the Request constructor, so that it is bound to the pipeline handler thread.

findings.condition: The request has cancelled_ set when doQueueRequest examines it.
findings.actor: PipelineHandler::doQueueRequest.
findings.timing: Queue insertion and post-increment sequence assignment precede completion and return.
findings.scope: The already-cancelled dispatch branch, including waiting requests processed during stop.
findings.reason: The branch calls completeRequest and returns before device submission or the later cancelRequest branch; the Korean and English claims agree with the source and peers.
findings.claim_quote: doQueueRequest는 요청을 data->queuedRequests_에 추가한 뒤, request->_d()->sequence_에 data->requestSequence_의 증가 전 값을 대입하고 그다음 data->requestSequence_를 증가시킵니다. doQueueRequest에서 request->_d()->cancelled_가 참이면 completeRequest(request)를 호출한 뒤 return으로 doQueueRequest 함수를 즉시 종료합니다. 따라서 이 분기는 queueRequestDevice 호출과 cancelRequest 처리보다 먼저 반환합니다.

findings.condition: The request has cancelled_ set when doQueueRequest examines it.
findings.actor: PipelineHandler::doQueueRequest.
findings.timing: Queue insertion and post-increment sequence assignment precede completion and return.
findings.scope: The already-cancelled dispatch branch, including waiting requests processed during stop.
findings.reason: The translation preserves the source's assignment, increment, early completion and return, and agrees with the Korean claim and dispatch peers.
findings.claim_quote: doQueueRequest adds the request to data->queuedRequests_, then assigns the pre-increment value of data->requestSequence_ to request->_d()->sequence_, and then increments data->requestSequence_. In doQueueRequest, if request->_d()->cancelled_ is true, it calls completeRequest(request) and then immediately ends the doQueueRequest function with return. Therefore, this branch returns before the queueRequestDevice call and the cancelRequest handling.

findings.condition: Already-cancelled requests return early; device submission applies to requests not already cancelled, with cancellation on a nonzero return.
findings.actor: PipelineHandler::doQueueRequest and the queueRequestDevice implementer.
findings.timing: Device programming is an implementer obligation for capture; failure handling follows the device queue call.
findings.scope: Common dispatch and device queue contract, rather than proof of actual device behavior.
findings.reason: The source supports both branches and the shall obligation. The UVC peers describe a particular implementation without changing the common contract.
findings.claim_quote: doQueueRequest는 request->_d()->cancelled_가 설정된 요청을 취소 분기에서 조기 반환시킨 뒤, 취소되지 않은 요청에 한해 queueRequestDevice(camera, request)를 호출하고 그 결과를 ret에 저장합니다. doQueueRequest에서 queueRequestDevice(camera, request)의 반환값 ret가 0이 아닐 때, 즉 if (ret) 조건이 참이면 cancelRequest(request)를 호출합니다. queueRequestDevice의 구현자는 요청에 포함된 매개변수가 요청에 제공된 버퍼에 캡처되는 프레임에 적용되도록 장치를 프로그래밍해야 합니다(shall). 요청은 스트림과 연결된 버퍼 집합과 매개변수 집합을 포함합니다.

findings.condition: Already-cancelled requests return early; device submission applies to requests not already cancelled, with cancellation on a nonzero return.
findings.actor: PipelineHandler::doQueueRequest and the queueRequestDevice implementer.
findings.timing: The cancellation decision follows the device queue return; programming applies to frames captured into request buffers.
findings.scope: Common source contract, not a measured device outcome.
findings.reason: The English claim preserves the Korean claim's branch conditions and mandatory programming obligation, consistent with the source and UVC-specific peers.
findings.claim_quote: doQueueRequest returns early in the cancellation branch for requests where request->_d()->cancelled_ is set. For requests that are not cancelled, it calls queueRequestDevice(camera, request) and stores the result in ret. In doQueueRequest, when the return value ret of queueRequestDevice(camera, request) is not 0, that is, when the if (ret) condition is true, it calls cancelRequest(request). The implementer of queueRequestDevice must program the device so that the parameters included in a request apply to the frames captured into the buffers provided with that request. A request contains a set of buffers associated with streams and a set of parameters.

findings.condition: cancelRequest is invoked on a pending request; internal cancellation acts on its pending buffers.
findings.actor: PipelineHandler::cancelRequest and Request::Private cancellation.
findings.timing: Each pending buffer is cancelled and its completion signal emitted during internal cancellation, before completeRequest is called.
findings.scope: Cancellation and completion processing; application return may wait for earlier requests.
findings.reason: The source establishes the stated call order and per-buffer effects. The stop peer describes a separate route through doQueueRequest, while the ordered-return peer explains possible notification delay.
findings.claim_quote: cancelRequest는 내부 cancel()을 호출한 뒤 completeRequest를 호출하여 요청을 완료합니다. 내부 취소는 각 대기 버퍼를 취소하고 해당 버퍼에 대해 bufferCompleted 신호를 발생시킵니다.

findings.condition: cancelRequest is called for a pending request; buffer operations apply to its pending buffers.
findings.actor: PipelineHandler::cancelRequest and Request::Private cancellation.
findings.timing: Internal cancellation and buffer signal emissions precede the call to completeRequest.

sources.source_quote:
\fn PipelineHandler::queueRequest()
 * \brief Queue a request
 * \param[in] request The request to queue
 *
 * This function queues a capture request to the pipeline handler for
 * processing. The request is first added to the internal list of waiting
 * requests which have to be prepared to make sure they are ready for being
 * queued to the pipeline handler.
 *
 * The queue of waiting requests is iterated and up to \a
 * maxQueuedRequestsDevice_ prepared requests are passed to the pipeline handler
 * in the same order they have been queued by calling this function.
 *
 * If a Request fails during the preparation phase or if the pipeline handler
 * fails in queuing the request to the hardware the request is cancelled.
 *
 * Keeping track of queued requests ensures automatic completion of all requests
 * when the pipeline handler is stopped with stop(). Request completion shall be
 * signalled by the pipeline handler using the completeRequest() function.
 *
 * \context This function is called from the CameraManager thread.
 */
void PipelineHandler::queueRequest(Request *request)
{
	LIBCAMERA_TRACEPOINT(request_queue, request);

	Camera *camera = request->_d()->camera();
	Camera::Private *data = camera->_d();
	data->waitingRequests_.push(request);

	request->_d()->prepare(300ms);
}

findings.claim_quote: 주석에 따르면 이 함수는 CameraManager 스레드에서 호출됩니다. PipelineHandler::queueRequest는 camera->_d()의 waitingRequests_에 request를 넣은 뒤, request->_d()->prepare(300ms)를 호출해 준비를 시작합니다. 주석은 준비 단계에서 Request가 실패하거나 파이프라인 핸들러가 하드웨어 큐잉에 실패하면 요청이 취소된다고 적고 있습니다.
