findings.reason: cancelled_에 따른 상태 선택과 큐 선두 및 pending 버퍼 확인은 제시된 소스에 근거한 관찰 항목입니다. 한영 비교 문장도 동일한 계획입니다.
findings.claim_quote: 소스 기반 조사 계획으로 `Request::Private::complete()`의 상태 대입 지점에서 `cancelled_`와 대입되는 상태를 대조합니다. 제출 큐의 선두와 pending 버퍼, 요청 완료 콜백도 관찰합니다.

findings.condition: 파이프라인 핸들러가 두 완료 API를 직접 호출하는 경우
findings.actor: 파이프라인 핸들러와 조사자
findings.timing: 변경 전후 호출 지점을 비교하며 각 API 호출 시 호출 스레드를 확인
findings.scope: API 호출 스레드 의무와 조사 계획; 실제 콜백 실행 스레드는 별도
findings.reason: 두 함수의 CameraManager 스레드 호출 의무가 소스와 일치하며, 한영 대응 문장도 의무와 조건을 보존합니다. 호출 스레드 의무만으로 콜백 실행 스레드를 확정하지 않습니다.
findings.claim_quote: 조사 계획은 기존 `completeBuffer`와 `completeRequest` 호출자 및 스레드 전달 경계를 찾아 변경 전후의 호출 위치를 대조하는 것입니다. 파이프라인 핸들러는 두 함수를 `CameraManager` 스레드에서 호출해야 합니다. 변경으로 다른 스레드에서 이 API를 직접 호출하면 문서화된 호출 의무와 충돌합니다.

findings.condition: 해당 소스 기반 조사 계획의 검증 범위를 설명하는 경우
findings.actor: 조사자
findings.timing: 계획 단계; 별도 실행 및 결정 자료 확인 전
findings.scope: 계획 자체의 한계이며 별도 가상 프로브 관찰의 부정이 아님
findings.reason: 완료 API 계약은 실제 제품의 콜백 스레드나 DMA 등을 검증하지 않습니다. 별도 프로브는 제한된 가상 환경의 실제 콜백 관찰이므로 이 계획의 한계와 충돌하지 않으며, 한영 문장도 그 범위를 유지합니다.

\brief Retrieve the request this buffer belongs to
 *
 * The intended callers of this function are buffer completion handlers that
 * need to associate a buffer to the request it belongs to.
 *
 * A FrameBuffer is associated to a request by Request::addBuffer() and the
 * association is valid until the buffer completes. The returned request
 * pointer is valid only during that interval.
 *
 * \return The Request the FrameBuffer belongs to, or nullptr if the buffer is
 * not associated with a request
 */
Request *FrameBuffer::request() const
{
	return _d()->request_;
}

\brief Add a FrameBuffer with its associated Stream to the Request
 * \param[in] stream The stream the buffer belongs to
 * \param[in] buffer The FrameBuffer to add to the request
 * \param[in] fence The optional fence
 *
 * A reference to the buffer is stored in the request. The caller is responsible
 * for ensuring that the buffer will remain valid until the request complete
 * callback is called.
 *
 * A request can only contain one buffer per stream. If a buffer has already
 * been added to the request for the same stream, this function returns -EEXIST.
 *
 * A Fence can be optionally associated with the \a buffer.
 *
 * When a valid Fence is provided to this function, \a fence is moved to \a
 * buffer and this Request will only be queued to the device once the
 * fences of all its buffers have been correctly signalled. Ownership of the
 * fence will only be taken in case of success, otherwise the fence will
 * be left unmodified.
 *
 * If the \a fence associated with \a buffer isn't signalled, the request will
 * fail after a timeout. The buffer will still contain the fence, which
 * applications must retrieve with FrameBuffer::releaseFence() before the buffer
 * can be reused in another request. Attempting to add a buffer that still
 * contains a fence to a request will result in this function returning -EEXIST.
 *
 * \sa FrameBuffer::releaseFence()
 *
 * \return 0 on success or a negative error code otherwise
 * \retval -EEXIST The request already contains a buffer for the stream
 *  or the buffer still references a fence
 * \retval -EINVAL The buffer does not reference a valid Stream
 */
int Request::addBuffer(const Stream *stream, FrameBuffer *buffer,

findings.claim_quote: 유효하게 dequeue된 버퍼의 `V4L2_BUF_FLAG_ERROR`와 FrameError를 기록하고, UVC가 해당 상태를 유지한 채 completeBuffer 다음에 completeRequest를 호출하는 경로를 확인합니다. pending에서 버퍼가 한 번 제거되는 횟수와 요청의 제출·완료 통지 순서, 요청 완료 콜백까지 버퍼가 유효하게 유지되는 수명을 기록하며, 다른 취소 원인이 없을 때 가능한 RequestComplete를 FrameError와 별도로 기록합니다.

findings.condition: 정상 정지와 STREAMOFF 또는 releaseBuffers 실패를 별도 사례로 다룹니다.
findings.actor: 조사자는 공통 정지 및 UVC 장치 경로를 추적합니다.
findings.timing: 대기 요청 분리 후 장치 정지와 대기 요청 취소를 살피고, 실패 후 후속 DQBUF도 조건부로 확인합니다.
findings.scope: 제출 순서에 따른 요청 반환과 버퍼별 처리 및 실패 경로의 관찰 계획입니다.
findings.reason: 정상 경로의 순서와 반환 계약에 부합합니다. 실패 시 성공이나 모든 버퍼 반환을 보장한다고 주장하지 않으며, cache 접근의 안전성도 미실행 확인 항목으로 둡니다. 한영 대응문도 같은 범위를 유지합니다.
findings.claim_quote: 정상 정지에서는 `waitingRequests_` 분리 후 장치 요청의 취소 완료, 분리된 요청의 순번 등록과 제출 순서에 따른 반환을 추적하고, 요청별·버퍼별 완료 횟수와 `queuedRequests_`·`waitingRequests_`의 잔존 및 정지 중 재투입을 기록합니다. STREAMOFF 실패와 releaseBuffers 실패를 별도 사례로 두고 각각의 ret, `state_`, `cache_`, `queuedBuffers_`, `queuedRequests_`, ASSERT 도달 및 정지 중 재투입을 기록하며, 실패 시 0 반환이나 모든 버퍼 반환을 기대하지 않고, STREAMOFF 실패 후 `cache_` reset과 잔존 notifier·큐가 겹치면 알려진 인덱스의 후속 DQBUF에서 `cache_`->put 접근이 안전하게 처리되는지 확인합니다.

findings.condition: 문서화된 재진입과 별도 허용이 없는 같은 함수의 콜백 중첩 진입을 구분합니다.
findings.actor: Signal 발신자는 전달 대상의 유효성을 유지하고, 요청 소유자는 지연 수신자의 마지막 사용을 조율합니다.
findings.timing: 실행 중 접근 검사를 통과한 stop의 Blocking 호출과 각 Queued 수신자의 이후 사용 종료를 별도로 확인합니다.
findings.scope: 수명과 스레드 경계에 관한 검증 계획이며 실제 콜백 실행 결과가 아닙니다.
findings.reason: 재귀 처리의 명시적 설명, 중첩 호출 제한, Blocking과 Queued의 차이 및 발신자의 수명 의무와 양립합니다. 모든 수신자와의 조율은 검증 계획이지 라이브러리의 자동 보장이 아닙니다. 영어 대응문도 이를 유지합니다.

// SPDX-License-Identifier: CC-BY-SA-4.0

/**
 * \page thread-safety Reentrancy and Thread-Safety
 *
 * Through the documentation, several terms are used to define how classes and
 * their member functions can be used from multiple threads.
 *
 * - A **reentrant** function may be called simultaneously from multiple
 *   threads if and only if each invocation uses a different instance of the
 *   class. This is the default for all member functions not explictly marked
 *   otherwise.
 *
 * - \anchor thread-safe A **thread-safe** function may be called
 *   simultaneously from multiple threads on the same instance of a class. A
 *   thread-safe function is thus reentrant. Thread-safe functions may also be
 *   called simultaneously with any other reentrant function of the same class
 *   on the same instance.
 *
 * \internal
 * - \anchor thread-bound A **thread-bound** function may be called only from
 *   the thread that the class instances lives in (see section \ref
 *   thread-objects). For instances of classes that do not derive from the
 *   Object class, this is the thread in which the instance was created. A
 *   thread-bound function is not thread-safe, and may or may not be reentrant.
 * \endinternal
 *
 * Neither reentrancy nor thread-safety, in this context, mean that a function
 * may be called simultaneously from the same thread, for instance from a
 * callback invoked by the function. This may deadlock and isn't allowed unless
 * separately documented.
 *
 * \if internal
 * A class is defined as reentrant, thread-safe or thread-bound if all its
 * member functions are reentrant, thread-safe or thread-bound respectively.
 * \else
 * A class is defined as reentrant or thread-safe if all its member functions
 * are reentrant or thread-safe respectively.
 * \endif
 * Some member functions may additionally be documented as having additional
 * thread-related attributes.
 *
 * Most classes are reentrant but not thread-safe, as making them fully
 * thread-safe would incur locking costs considered prohibitive for the
 * expected use cases.
 */

\class Signal
 * \brief Generic signal and slot communication mechanism
 *
 * Signals and slots are a language construct aimed at communication between
 * objects through the observer pattern without the need for boilerplate code.
 * See http://doc.qt.io/qt-6/signalsandslots.html for more information.
 *
 * Signals model events that can be observed from objects unrelated to the event
 * source. Slots are functions that are called in response to a signal. Signals
 * can be connected to and disconnected from slots dynamically at runtime. When
 * a signal is emitted, all connected slots are called sequentially in the order
 * they have been connected.
 *
 * Signals are defined with zero, one or more typed parameters. They are emitted
 * with a value for each of the parameters, and those values are passed to the
 * connected slots.
 *
 * Slots are normal static or class member functions. In order to be connected
 * to a signal, their signature must match the signal type (taking the same
 * arguments as the signal and returning void).
 *
 * Connecting a signal to a slot results in the slot being called with the
 * arguments passed to the emit() function when the signal is emitted. Multiple
 * slots can be connected to the same signal, and multiple signals can connected
 * to the same slot.
 *
 * When a slot belongs to an instance of the Object class, the slot is called
 * in the context of the thread that the object is bound to. If the signal is
 * emitted from the same thread, the slot will be called synchronously, before
 * Signal::emit() returns. If the signal is emitted from a different thread,
 * the slot will be called asynchronously from the object's thread's event
 * loop, after the Signal::emit() function returns, with a copy of the signal's
 * arguments. The emitter shall thus ensure that any pointer or reference
 * passed through the signal will remain valid after the signal is emitted.
 *
 * Duplicate connections between a signal and a slot are not expected and use of
 * the Object class to manage signals will enforce this restriction.
 */

\brief Create a request object for the camera

 * buffers and parameters, and queue for capture.

 * The \a cookie is stored in the request and is accessible through the
 * Request::cookie() function at any time. It is typically used by applications
 * to map the request to an external resource in the request completion
 * handler, and is completely opaque to libcamera.

findings.claim_quote: 허용된 doQueueRequests 재진입에서는 pop과 투입 순서 및 request별 투입 횟수를 기록해 중복 투입이 없는지 확인하고, 같은 함수의 콜백 중첩 진입은 별도 허용 문서 없이 하지 않습니다. Direct와 지연된 Queued 수신의 현재·수신 스레드, cookie, sequence, 콜백 진입·복귀, stop 전후와 객체 수명을 기록하며, 실행 중 접근 검사를 통과한 `Camera::stop`이 `PipelineHandler::stop`을 ConnectionTypeBlocking으로 호출하는 정상 경로에 해당 실행이 도달했는지와 Blocking 반환 및 별도 Queued 수신자의 마지막 사용·종료를 구분해 확인하고, `Signal` 발신자가 포인터·참조의 유효성을 유지하며 요청 소유자가 삭제·재사용 전에 모든 지연 수신자의 마지막 사용을 완료·해제 협의로 동기화하는지 검증하고 요청 완료 신호나 한 핸들러의 복귀를 모든 지연 수신자의 사용 종료로 간주하지 않습니다.

findings.condition: stop과 상태 영향 함수의 동기화 및 게시된 메서드의 실제 실행 조건을 대조합니다.
findings.actor: 호출자는 상태 변경을 동기화하고 버퍼를 유효하게 유지하며, 파이프라인 핸들러는 완료 후 요청 접근 제한을 따릅니다.
findings.timing: 메시지 게시부터 정지와 상태 검사까지의 상대 순서 및 완료 함수 반환 후를 구분합니다.
findings.scope: 정지 경합과 ASSERT 전제에 대한 시험 계획입니다.
findings.reason: stop의 호출자 동기화 의무, 큐 게시 경로, 핸들러의 요청 접근 제한 및 버퍼 수명 계약에 부합합니다. 정지 뒤 실행은 조건부 시험으로 분류하며 발생을 단정하지 않습니다. 영어 대응문도 의무와 조건을 보존합니다.

findings.actor: 호출 스레드들과 파이프라인, 각 신호 수신 연결을 구분합니다.
findings.timing: 호출 시작, 메시지 게시, 큐 등록, 통지, 콜백 진입과 복귀를 각각 기록합니다.
findings.scope: 순서와 식별자의 상관관계에 대한 조사 계획입니다.
findings.reason: 소스의 잠금 내 게시와 큐 등록 및 완료 통지 경로에 맞춰 서로 다른 사건을 구분합니다. 호출 시작 순서나 두 sequence의 동일성을 가정하지 않으며 한영 대응문이 일치합니다.
findings.claim_quote: 서로 다른 `Request`와 버퍼로 동시 제출하면서 `Request` 식별자와 cookie, 호출 스레드별 queueRequest 시작·반환값, `Thread::postMessage`의 mutex 안 `list_` 추가 순서, `PipelineHandler::queueRequest` 진입과 `waitingRequests_` 등록 순서를 추가 계측해 연관 기록합니다. doQueueRequest의 `Request` sequence와 `queuedRequests_` 선두에서의 requestComplete 통지 순서, bufferReady·bufferCompleted·requestCompleted 신호 발생 및 특정 연결의 콜백 진입·복귀를 각각 기록하며, `Request` sequence와 `FrameMetadata` sequence의 동일성이나 서로 다른 스레드의 호출 시작에 관한 전역 순서는 가정하지 않습니다.

findings.condition: 준비 대기와 장치 대기 요청을 섞고 두 실패를 각각 주입하는 조사입니다.
findings.actor: 조사자는 PipelineHandler 정지와 UVC 장치 정지 경로의 기존 호출을 관찰합니다.
findings.timing: 경로 변경 후 정지 및 취소 콜백 재진입을 포함해 반환값과 분기를 기록합니다.
findings.scope: 실패 주입 및 재진입에 대한 계획이며 실제 실행이나 성공을 주장하지 않습니다.
findings.reason: 공통 정지의 큐 분리와 UVC의 streamOff 및 releaseBuffers 호출에 근거한 관찰 항목입니다. requestBuffers 반환값 관찰은 해당 호출에 도달하는 경우에 적용되며, 한영 대응문이 같은 계획을 서술합니다.
findings.claim_quote: 조사 계획으로, 선택 경로를 바꾼 뒤 준비 대기와 장치 대기 요청을 섞어 `PipelineHandler::stop()`을 실행하고 취소 콜백이 재진입하는 경우를 포함하여, 요청별 완료 횟수와 제출 순서, `waitingRequests_`와 `queuedRequests_`의 잔존 여부, 정지 후 재투입 여부를 기록합니다. 또한 `PipelineHandlerUVC::stopDevice()` 경로에서 `VIDIOC_STREAMOFF`와 `releaseBuffers()`의 실패를 각각 주입하고, 기존 호출에서 반환값과 `streamOff()`의 후속 분기, `releaseBuffers()`의 `requestBuffers(0, memoryType_)` 반환값을 관찰하여 기록합니다.

findings.condition: Auto가 서로 다른 스레드로 인해 Queued를 선택했고 완료 함수 반환 및 큐 비움 뒤에도 콜백 진입 기록이 없는 경우입니다.
findings.actor: 조사자는 실제 제품 애플리케이션의 수신 스레드와 메시지 처리 경로를 확인합니다.
findings.timing: 완료 함수 반환 이후의 누락된 콜백 기록을 조건으로 조사합니다.
findings.scope: 이벤트 루프 미처리 가능성에 대한 미실행 조사 계획입니다.
findings.reason: Queued 선택 및 비동기 전달 경로와 양립하며, 기록 부재의 원인을 확정하거나 제품 콜백이 실행됐다고 주장하지 않습니다. 별도의 가상 프로브 관측은 다른 실행 범위이므로 이 제품 조사 계획과 충돌하지 않습니다. 영어 대응문도 가능성과 조건을 유지합니다.

\page thread Thread Support
 *
 * libcamera supports multi-threaded applications through a threading model that
 * sets precise rules to guarantee thread-safe usage of the API. Additionally,
 * libcamera makes internal use of threads, and offers APIs that simplify
 * interactions with application threads. Careful compliance with the threading
 * model will ensure avoidance of race conditions.
 *
 * Every thread created by libcamera is associated with an instance of the
 * Thread class. Those threads run an internal event loop by default to
 * dispatch events to objects. Additionally, the main thread of the application
 * (defined as the thread that calls CameraManager::start()) is also associated
 * with a Thread instance, but has no event loop accessible to libcamera. Other
 * application threads are not visible to libcamera.
 *
 * \section thread-objects Threads and Objects
 *
 * Instances of the Object class and all its derived classes are thread-aware
 * and are bound to the thread they are created in. They are said to *live* in
 * a thread, and they interact with the event loop of their thread for the
 * purpose of message passing and signal delivery. Messages posted to the
 * object with Object::postMessage() will be delivered from the event loop of
 * the thread that the object lives in. Signals delivered to the object, unless
 * explicitly connected with ConnectionTypeDirect, will also be delivered from
 * the object thread's event loop.
 *
 * All Object instances created internally by libcamera are bound to internal
 * threads. As objects interact with thread event loops for proper operation,
 * creating an Object instance in a thread that has no internal event loop (such
 * as the main application thread, or libcamera threads that have a custom main
 * loop), prevents some features of the Object class from being used. See
 * Thread::exec() for more details.
 *
 * \section thread-signals Threads and Signals
 *
 * When sent to a receiver that does not inherit from the Object class, signals
 * are delivered synchronously in the thread of the sender. When the receiver
 * inherits from the Object class, delivery is by default asynchronous if the
 * sender and receiver live in different threads. In that case, the signal is
 * posted to the receiver's message queue and will be delivered from the
 * receiver's event loop, running in the receiver's thread. This mechanism can
 * be overridden by selecting a different connection type when calling
 * Signal::connect().
 */

\brief Add a FrameBuffer with its associated Stream to the Request
 * \param[in] stream The stream the buffer belongs to
 * \param[in] buffer The FrameBuffer to add to the request
 * \param[in] fence The optional fence
 *
 * A reference to the buffer is stored in the request. The caller is responsible
 * for ensuring that the buffer will remain valid until the request complete
 * callback is called.
 *
 * A request can only contain one buffer per stream. If a buffer has already
 * been added to the request for the same stream, this function returns -EEXIST.
 *
 * A Fence can be optionally associated with the \a buffer.
 *
 * When a valid Fence is provided to this function, \a fence is moved to \a
 * buffer and this Request will only be queued to the device once the
 * fences of all its buffers have been correctly signalled. Ownership of the
 * fence will only be taken in case of success, otherwise the fence will
 * be left unmodified.
 *
 * If the \a fence associated with \a buffer isn't signalled, the request will
 * fail after a timeout. The buffer will still contain the fence, which
 * applications must retrieve with FrameBuffer::releaseFence() before the buffer
 * can be reused in another request. Attempting to add a buffer that still
 * contains a fence to a request will result in this function returning -EEXIST.
 *
 * \sa FrameBuffer::releaseFence()
 *
 * \return 0 on success or a negative error code otherwise
 * \retval -EEXIST The request already contains a buffer for the stream
 *  or the buffer still references a fence
 * \retval -EINVAL The buffer does not reference a valid Stream
 */
int Request::addBuffer(const Stream *stream, FrameBuffer *buffer,

findings.claim_quote: `Request::addBuffer`는 버퍼에 대한 참조를 요청에 저장합니다. 호출자는 요청 완료 콜백이 호출될 때까지 해당 버퍼가 유효하게 남아 있도록 보장해야 합니다.

findings.condition: 검사를 통과하는 성공 경로입니다.
findings.actor: Camera가 파이프라인 핸들러에 queued 호출을 게시하고 완료 신호를 발생시킵니다.
findings.timing: invokeMethod 호출 후 0을 반환하며 요청 완료는 별도로 통지합니다.
findings.scope: 호출 게시와 반환의 순서입니다. 파이프라인 메서드나 콜백이 0 반환 전후 어느 때 실행되는지는 보장하지 않습니다.
findings.reason: 코드와 한영 비교 문장은 성공 반환과 요청 완료를 구분합니다. queued 호출은 수신 실행을 기다리지 않습니다.
findings.claim_quote: `Camera::queueRequest()`는 요청 검사를 마친 뒤 `ConnectionTypeQueued`를 지정해 `invokeMethod`로 `PipelineHandler::queueRequest`를 호출하고, 그 호출 뒤에 `0`을 반환합니다. 이 `0`은 `invokeMethod` 호출 뒤의 반환값이며, 요청 완료는 카메라가 `requestCompleted` 신호로 별도로 알립니다.

findings.condition: 파이프라인 핸들러가 완료된 요청에 대해 함수를 호출하는 경우입니다.
findings.actor: 파이프라인 핸들러가 호출하고 completeRequest가 애플리케이션 반환 순서를 보장합니다.
findings.timing: 함수 호출 순서에는 제약이 없지만 요청 반환은 제출 순서를 따릅니다.
findings.scope: 함수 호출 순서와 요청 객체의 애플리케이션 반환 순서는 서로 다른 사건입니다.
findings.reason: 소스의 API 계약과 한영 비교 문장이 반환 순서의 보장과 호출 순서의 자유를 구분합니다.

findings.reason: 두 함수의 문서화된 호출 문맥이 일치하고 한영 비교 문장도 호출 스레드와 콜백 실행 스레드를 구분합니다.

\brief Complete a buffer for a request
 * \param[in] request The request the buffer belongs to
 * \param[in] buffer The buffer that has completed
 *
 * This function shall be called by pipeline handlers to signal completion of
 * the \a buffer part of the \a request. It notifies applications of buffer
 * completion and updates the request's internal buffer tracking. The request
 * is not completed automatically when the last buffer completes to give
 * pipeline handlers a chance to perform any operation that may still be
 * needed. They shall complete requests explicitly with completeRequest().
 *
 * \context This function shall be called from the CameraManager thread.
 *
 * \return True if all buffers contained in the request have completed, false
 * otherwise
 */
bool PipelineHandler::completeBuffer(Request *request, FrameBuffer *buffer)
{
	Camera *camera = request->_d()->camera();
	camera->bufferCompleted.emit(request, buffer);
	return request->_d()->completeBuffer(buffer);
}

/**
 * \brief Signal request completion

findings.claim_quote: completeBuffer와 completeRequest는 모두 `CameraManager` 스레드에서 호출해야 합니다.

findings.condition: registerRequest가 연결한 prepared 신호의 람다가 호출되는 경우입니다.
findings.actor: 파이프라인 핸들러에 연결된 람다가 doQueueRequests를 호출합니다.
findings.timing: prepared 신호 수신 시 호출됩니다.
findings.scope: 등록된 람다의 호출 대상에 관한 설명입니다.
findings.reason: 등록 코드에서 람다가 요청의 카메라를 인수로 doQueueRequests를 호출하며 비교 문장도 해당 연결을 식별합니다.
findings.claim_quote: `PipelineHandler::registerRequest()`에서 request->`_d()`->prepared 신호에 연결된 람다 콜백이 실제로 호출하는 함수는 doQueueRequests입니다.

findings.condition: 대기할 fence가 없거나, fence가 있고 선택적 timeout이 0이 아닌 경우를 구분합니다.
findings.actor: Request의 private 준비 로직이 notifier와 필요한 timer를 설정하고 취소를 처리합니다.
findings.timing: 대기할 fence가 없으면 즉시 prepared를 발생시킵니다. 대기 중 timeout이 만료되면 취소 후 prepared를 발생시킵니다.
findings.scope: 준비 단계와 타이머의 스레드 바인딩에 관한 소스 동작이며 촬영이나 정지 완료 시간의 보장은 아닙니다.
findings.reason: 준비 코드와 timeout 처리 경로가 notifier, 즉시 반환, 조건부 timer 생성과 취소 순서를 뒷받침합니다. 한영 비교 계획도 준비 취소 경로를 조사 대상으로 구분합니다.
findings.claim_quote: `Request::Private::prepare`는 `pending_`에 있는 각 `FrameBuffer`의 획득 펜스마다 fd를 읽기 대기하는 `EventNotifier`를 만들어 연결하며, 펜스가 신호되면 notifierActivated가 호출됩니다. 대기할 펜스가 없으면 `notifiers_`가 비어 있게 되므로 `Request::prepared` 신호를 즉시 발생시키고 바로 반환합니다. 선택적 timeout 인자가 0ms가 아니고 대기할 펜스가 있을 때에만 `Timer`를 만들어 timeout 시간으로 시작하며, 만료 시점에 모든 펜스가 올바르게 신호되지 않았다면 `Request`가 취소되고 `Request::prepared` 신호가 발생합니다. 이 타이머는 `Request` 생성자가 아니라 prepare 호출 시점에 만들어지는데, 파이프라인 핸들러 스레드에 바인딩되도록 하기 위해서입니다.

findings.condition: 큐 선두가 Pending인지에 따라 분기합니다.
findings.actor: PipelineHandler::completeRequest()가 카메라의 요청 큐를 순회합니다.
findings.timing: Pending이면 순회를 중단하고, 그렇지 않으면 검사 후 제거와 통지를 차례로 수행합니다.
findings.scope: 요청 반환 순서와 함수 호출 순서에 관한 소스 계약이며 콜백 실행 관측은 아닙니다.
findings.reason: 선두의 Pending 분기, 부정 조건 ASSERT, pop_front 및 requestComplete 호출 순서가 소스와 관련 문서의 설명에 부합합니다.
findings.claim_quote: `completeRequest()`의 조사에서는 큐 선두 요청의 상태가 `Request::RequestPending`인지 관찰합니다. 해당 상태이면 `break`로 반복문을 벗어나 선두 요청이 큐에 남고, 제출 순서에 따라 뒤에서 이미 완료된 요청도 `requestComplete()`로 반환되지 않는 분기를 살펴봅니다. 선두가 해당 상태가 아니면 `ASSERT(!req->hasPendingBuffers());`가 대기 중인 버퍼가 없다는 부정 조건을 검사한 뒤 `pop_front()`로 선두를 제거하고 `requestComplete(req)`를 호출하는 순서를 관찰합니다.

findings.condition: 카메라를 해제하기 전에는 재시작과 재구성이 가능하며, 필요한 경우 동기화해야 합니다.
findings.actor: 애플리케이션이 카메라를 운영하고 호출자가 상태 변경 함수의 동기화를 책임집니다.
findings.timing: 촬영 전 확보·구성·시작하고 사용을 마치면 해제합니다.
findings.scope: 카메라 운영과 상태 변경 함수의 호출자 책임에 관한 계약입니다.
findings.reason: 한영 표현은 의무, 가능성 및 조건부 동기화 책임을 보존하며 관련 소스와 일치합니다.

sources.source_quote:
An application needs to perform a sequence of operations on a camera before
 * it is ready to process requests. The camera needs to be acquired and
 * configured to prepare the camera for capture. Once started the camera can
 * process requests until it is stopped. When an application is done with a
 * camera, the camera needs to be released.

An application may start and stop a camera multiple times as long as it is
 * not released. The camera may also be reconfigured.

Functions that affect the camera state as defined below are generally not
 * synchronized with each other by the Camera class. The caller is responsible
 * for ensuring their synchronization if necessary.

findings.claim_quote: 애플리케이션은 촬영을 준비하기 위해 카메라를 확보하고 구성한 뒤 시작해야 하며, 시작된 카메라는 정지할 때까지 요청을 처리할 수 있고, 애플리케이션은 사용을 마치면 카메라를 해제해야 합니다. 애플리케이션은 카메라를 해제하지 않은 동안 여러 번 시작하고 정지할 수 있으며, 카메라를 재구성할 수도 있습니다. Camera 클래스는 카메라 상태에 영향을 주는 함수들을 일반적으로 서로 동기화하지 않으므로, 필요한 경우 호출자가 이 함수들의 동기화를 책임져야 합니다.

findings.condition: 재시작은 해제 전이며 동기화 책임은 필요한 경우에 적용됩니다.
findings.actor: 애플리케이션과 상태 변경 함수의 호출자입니다.
findings.timing: 확보와 구성 후 시작하고 사용 종료 시 해제합니다.
findings.scope: 카메라 운영 및 호출자 동기화 책임입니다.
findings.reason: 영문은 한국어와 동일한 의무와 가능성을 표현하며 소스의 일반적 동기화 한계를 유지합니다.

findings.claim_quote: To prepare for capture, the application must acquire and configure the camera, then start it. A started camera can process requests until it is stopped. When the application is done with the camera, it must release the camera. As long as the camera has not been released, the application may start and stop it multiple times and may also reconfigure it. The Camera class generally does not synchronize functions that affect the camera state with each other, so the caller must take responsibility for synchronizing these functions when necessary.

findings.timing: 확보와 카메라 생성·등록 후 성공을 반환하며, 성공 반환 후 새 인스턴스의 match()가 호출됩니다.
findings.scope: 미디어 장치 확보·해제 의무와 CameraManager 호출 스레드입니다.

sources.source_quote:
\fn PipelineHandler::match(DeviceEnumerator *enumerator)
 * \brief Match media devices and create camera instances
 * \param[in] enumerator The enumerator providing all media devices found in the
 * system
 *
 * This function is the main entry point of the pipeline handler. It is called
 * by the camera manager with the \a enumerator passed as an argument. It shall
 * acquire from the \a enumerator all the media devices it needs for a single
 * pipeline, create one or multiple Camera instances and register them with the
 * camera manager.
 *
 * If all media devices needed by the pipeline handler are found, they must all
 * be acquired by a call to MediaDevice::acquire(). This function shall then
 * create the corresponding Camera instances, store them internally, and return
 * true. Otherwise it shall not acquire any media device (or shall release all
 * the media devices is has acquired by calling MediaDevice::release()) and
 * return false.
 *
 * If multiple instances of a pipeline are available in the system, the
 * PipelineHandler class will be instantiated once per instance, and its match()
 * function called for every instance. Each call shall acquire media devices for
 * one pipeline instance, until all compatible media devices are exhausted.
 *
 * If this function returns true, a new instance of the pipeline handler will
 * be created and its match() function called.
 *
 * \context This function is called from the CameraManager thread.
 *
 * \return true if media devices have been acquired and camera instances
 * created, or false otherwise
 */

findings.claim_quote: PipelineHandler::match() 구현자는 단일 파이프라인에 필요한 모든 미디어 장치를 찾으면 MediaDevice::acquire()를 호출해 장치를 모두 확보한 뒤 해당 Camera 인스턴스를 하나 이상 생성하고 내부에 저장하며 카메라 매니저에 등록한 후 true를 반환해야 합니다. PipelineHandler::match() 구현자는 필요한 미디어 장치를 모두 찾지 못한 경우 아직 장치를 확보하지 않았다면 어떤 미디어 장치도 확보해서는 안 되며, 이미 일부를 확보했다면 확보한 장치를 모두 MediaDevice::release()로 해제하고 false를 반환해야 합니다. PipelineHandler::match()는 CameraManager 스레드에서 호출되며, true를 반환하면 새 PipelineHandler 인스턴스가 생성되고 그 인스턴스의 match()가 호출됩니다.

findings.condition: 필요한 장치를 모두 찾은 경우와 일부를 찾지 못한 경우를 구분합니다.
findings.actor: PipelineHandler::match() 구현자와 카메라 매니저입니다.
findings.timing: 장치 확보 및 카메라 생성·등록 후 true를 반환하고, true 반환 후 새 인스턴스를 호출합니다.
findings.scope: 단일 파이프라인의 장치 확보와 실패 시 해제 및 호출 스레드입니다.
findings.reason: 영문은 한국어와 같은 확보·해제 의무와 실패 조건을 유지하며 소스에 부합합니다.

sources.source_quote:
\fn PipelineHandler::match(DeviceEnumerator *enumerator)
 * \brief Match media devices and create camera instances
 * \param[in] enumerator The enumerator providing all media devices found in the
 * system
 *
 * This function is the main entry point of the pipeline handler. It is called
 * by the camera manager with the \a enumerator passed as an argument. It shall
 * acquire from the \a enumerator all the media devices it needs for a single
 * pipeline, create one or multiple Camera instances and register them with the
 * camera manager.
 *
 * If all media devices needed by the pipeline handler are found, they must all
 * be acquired by a call to MediaDevice::acquire(). This function shall then
 * create the corresponding Camera instances, store them internally, and return
 * true. Otherwise it shall not acquire any media device (or shall release all
 * the media devices is has acquired by calling MediaDevice::release()) and
 * return false.
 *
 * If multiple instances of a pipeline are available in the system, the
 * PipelineHandler class will be instantiated once per instance, and its match()
 * function called for every instance. Each call shall acquire media devices for
 * one pipeline instance, until all compatible media devices are exhausted.
 *
 * If this function returns true, a new instance of the pipeline handler will
 * be created and its match() function called.
 *
 * \context This function is called from the CameraManager thread.
 *
 * \return true if media devices have been acquired and camera instances
 * created, or false otherwise
 */

findings.claim_quote: When all media devices needed for a single pipeline are found, the implementer of PipelineHandler::match() must call MediaDevice::acquire() to acquire all of them, create one or more corresponding Camera instances, store them internally, register them with the camera manager, and then return true. If not all required media devices are found, the implementer of PipelineHandler::match() must not acquire any media device when none has yet been acquired; when some devices have already been acquired, the implementer must release all of them with MediaDevice::release() and return false. PipelineHandler::match() is called on the CameraManager thread. If PipelineHandler::match() returns true, a new PipelineHandler instance is created and match() is called on that instance.

findings.condition: 요청된 roles의 충족 가능 여부에 따라 유효한 구성 또는 null을 반환합니다.
findings.actor: 호출자는 roles를 채우고 PipelineHandler 구현자는 스레드 안전성을 갖춰야 합니다.
findings.timing: 기본 구성 생성 호출 시 적용되며 어느 스레드에서든 호출될 수 있습니다.
findings.scope: PipelineHandler::generateConfiguration()의 입력, 반환 및 스레드 계약입니다.
findings.reason: 기본 구성의 내용과 조건부 반환, 임의 스레드 호출 가능성 및 스레드 안전 의무가 소스와 일치합니다.

sources.source_quote:
\fn PipelineHandler::generateConfiguration()
 * \brief Generate a camera configuration for a specified camera
 * \param[in] camera The camera to generate a default configuration for
 * \param[in] roles A list of stream roles
 *
 * Generate a default configuration for the \a camera for a specified list of
 * stream roles. The caller shall populate the \a roles with the use-cases it
 * wishes to fetch the default configuration for. The returned configuration
 * can then be examined by the caller to learn about the selected streams and
 * their default parameters.
 *
 * The intended companion to this is \a configure() which can be used to change
 * the group of streams parameters.
 *
 * \context This function may be called from any thread and shall be
 * \threadsafe. It shall not modify the state of the \a camera in the pipeline
 * handler.
 *
 * \return A valid CameraConfiguration if the requested roles can be satisfied,
 * or a null pointer otherwise.
 */

findings.claim_quote: generateConfiguration 호출자는 기본 구성을 가져오려는 사용 사례를 roles에 채워야 합니다. generateConfiguration()이 반환하는 구성에는 선택된 스트림과 각 스트림의 기본 파라미터 정보가 포함됩니다. PipelineHandler::generateConfiguration()은 요청된 roles를 충족할 수 있으면 유효한 CameraConfiguration을 반환해야 하고, 그렇지 않으면 null 포인터를 반환해야 합니다. PipelineHandler::generateConfiguration()은 어떤 스레드에서든 호출될 수 있으므로, 구현은 스레드 안전성을 갖춰야 합니다.

findings.condition: Requested roles are satisfiable or unsatisfiable, respectively.
findings.actor: The caller populates roles; the pipeline handler implements generateConfiguration().
findings.timing: At configuration generation, callable from any thread.
findings.scope: Default configuration and the function's thread-safety contract.
findings.reason: The return conditions, caller obligation, configuration contents and thread-safety requirement match the source. The source also prohibits changing camera state, but the claim does not assert otherwise.

The configuration returned by generateConfiguration() includes the selected streams and the default parameter information for each stream. PipelineHandler::generateConfiguration() must return a valid CameraConfiguration if the requested roles can be satisfied; otherwise, it must return a null pointer. PipelineHandler::generateConfiguration() may be called from any thread, so the implementation must be threadsafe.

sources.source_quote:
\fn PipelineHandler::configure()
 * \brief Configure a group of streams for capture
 * \param[in] camera The camera to configure
 * \param[in] config The camera configurations to setup
 *
 * Configure the specified group of streams for \a camera according to the
 * configuration specified in \a config. The intended caller of this interface
 * is the Camera class which will receive configuration to apply from the
 * application.
 *
 * The configuration is guaranteed to have been validated with
 * CameraConfiguration::validate(). The pipeline handler implementation shall
 * not perform further validation and may rely on any custom field stored in its
 * custom CameraConfiguration derived class.
 *
 * When configuring the camera the pipeline handler shall associate a Stream
 * instance to each StreamConfiguration entry in the CameraConfiguration using
 * the StreamConfiguration::setStream() function.
 *
 * \context This function is called from the CameraManager thread.
 *
 * \return 0 on success or a negative error code otherwise
 */

findings.claim_quote: PipelineHandler::configure()는 CameraManager 스레드에서 호출되며, 구현은 성공하면 0을 반환하고 실패하면 음수 오류 코드를 반환해야 합니다.

findings.condition: A pipeline handler signals completion of a request buffer.
findings.actor: The pipeline handler calls completeBuffer() and explicitly completes the request.
findings.timing: queueRequestDevice() and completeBuffer() are called on the CameraManager thread; buffer completion alone does not complete the request.
findings.scope: API call context and notification contract, not the actual callback execution thread.

sources.source_quote:
\fn PipelineHandler::queueRequestDevice()
 * \brief Queue a request to the device
 * \param[in] camera The camera to queue the request to
 * \param[in] request The request to queue
 *
 * This function queues a capture request to the device for processing. The
 * request contains a set of buffers associated with streams and a set of
 * parameters. The pipeline handler shall program the device to ensure that the
 * parameters will be applied to the frames captured in the buffers provided in
 * the request.
 *
 * \context This function is called from the CameraManager thread.
 *
 * \return 0 on success or a negative error code otherwise
 */

\brief Complete a buffer for a request
 * \param[in] request The request the buffer belongs to
 * \param[in] buffer The buffer that has completed
 *
 * This function shall be called by pipeline handlers to signal completion of
 * the \a buffer part of the \a request. It notifies applications of buffer
 * completion and updates the request's internal buffer tracking. The request
 * is not completed automatically when the last buffer completes to give
 * pipeline handlers a chance to perform any operation that may still be
 * needed. They shall complete requests explicitly with completeRequest().
 *
 * \context This function shall be called from the CameraManager thread.
 *
 * \return True if all buffers contained in the request have completed, false
 * otherwise
 */
bool PipelineHandler::completeBuffer

findings.claim_quote: PipelineHandler::queueRequestDevice()는 CameraManager 스레드에서 호출됩니다. 파이프라인 핸들러는 요청의 버퍼 완료를 알리기 위해 CameraManager 스레드에서 completeBuffer()를 호출해야 합니다. 이 함수는 애플리케이션에 버퍼 완료를 통지하고 요청 내부의 버퍼 추적 정보를 갱신합니다. 마지막 버퍼가 완료되어도 요청은 자동으로 완료되지 않으므로 파이프라인 핸들러는 completeRequest()를 명시적으로 호출해 요청을 완료해야 합니다.

findings.condition: A pipeline handler signals completion of a request buffer.
findings.actor: The pipeline handler calls completeBuffer() and explicitly completes the request.
findings.timing: queueRequestDevice() and completeBuffer() are called on the CameraManager thread; the last buffer does not automatically complete the request.
findings.scope: API call context and notification contract, not the actual callback execution thread.
findings.reason: The English translation preserves the Korean claim's obligations and distinction between buffer and request completion. The lifecycle peers specify compatible signal and callback details.

\brief Create a request object for the camera
 * \param[in] cookie Opaque cookie for application use
 *
 * This function creates an empty request for the application to fill with
 * buffers and parameters, and queue for capture.
 *
 * The \a cookie is stored in the request and is accessible through the
 * Request::cookie() function at any time. It is typically used by applications
 * to map the request to an external resource in the request completion
 * handler, and is completely opaque to libcamera.
 *
 * The ownership of the returned request is passed to the caller, which is
 * responsible for deleting it. The request may be deleted in the completion
 * handler, or reused after resetting its state with Request::reuse().
 *
 * \context This function is \threadsafe. It may only be called when the camera
 * is in the Configured or Running state as defined in \ref camera_operation.
 *
 * \return A pointer to the newly created request, or nullptr on error
 */
std::unique_ptr<Request> Camera::createRequest(uint64_t cookie)

// SPDX-License-Identifier: CC-BY-SA-4.0

/**
 * \page thread-safety Reentrancy and Thread-Safety
 *
 * Through the documentation, several terms are used to define how classes and
 * their member functions can be used from multiple threads.
 *
 * - A **reentrant** function may be called simultaneously from multiple
 *   threads if and only if each invocation uses a different instance of the
 *   class. This is the default for all member functions not explictly marked
 *   otherwise.
 *
 * - \anchor thread-safe A **thread-safe** function may be called
 *   simultaneously from multiple threads on the same instance of a class. A
 *   thread-safe function is thus reentrant. Thread-safe functions may also be
 *   called simultaneously with any other reentrant function of the same class
 *   on the same instance.
 *
 * \internal
 * - \anchor thread-bound A **thread-bound** function may be called only from
 *   the thread that the class instances lives in (see section \ref
 *   thread-objects). For instances of classes that do not derive from the
 *   Object class, this is the thread in which the instance was created. A
 *   thread-bound function is not thread-safe, and may or may not be reentrant.
 * \endinternal
 *
 * Neither reentrancy nor thread-safety, in this context, mean that a function
 * may be called simultaneously from the same thread, for instance from a
 * callback invoked by the function. This may deadlock and isn't allowed unless
 * separately documented.
 *
 * \if internal
 * A class is defined as reentrant, thread-safe or thread-bound if all its
 * member functions are reentrant, thread-safe or thread-bound respectively.
 * \else
 * A class is defined as reentrant or thread-safe if all its member functions
 * are reentrant or thread-safe respectively.
 * \endif
 * Some member functions may additionally be documented as having additional
 * thread-related attributes.
 *
 * Most classes are reentrant but not thread-safe, as making them fully
 * thread-safe would incur locking costs considered prohibitive for the
 * expected use cases.
 */

/**
 * \page thread-safety Reentrancy and Thread-Safety
 *
 * Through the documentation, several terms are used to define how classes and
 * their member functions can be used from multiple threads.
 *
 * - A **reentrant** function may be called simultaneously from multiple
 *   threads if and only if each invocation uses a different instance of the
 *   class. This is the default for all member functions not explictly marked
 *   otherwise.
 *
 * - \anchor thread-safe A **thread-safe** function may be called
 *   simultaneously from multiple threads on the same instance of a class. A

 *   called simultaneously with any other reentrant function of the same class
 *   on the same instance.
 *

 *   the thread that the class instances lives in (see section \ref
 *   thread-objects). For instances of classes that do not derive from the
 *   Object class, this is the thread in which the instance was created. A
 *   thread-bound function is not thread-safe, and may or may not be reentrant.
 * \endinternal
 *

 * may be called simultaneously from the same thread, for instance from a
 * callback invoked by the function. This may deadlock and isn't allowed unless

\brief Create a request object for the camera
 * \param[in] cookie Opaque cookie for application use
 *
 * This function creates an empty request for the application to fill with
 * buffers and parameters, and queue for capture.
 *
 * The \a cookie is stored in the request and is accessible through the
 * Request::cookie() function at any time. It is typically used by applications
 * to map the request to an external resource in the request completion
 * handler, and is completely opaque to libcamera.
 *
 * The ownership of the returned request is passed to the caller, which is
 * responsible for deleting it. The request may be deleted in the completion
 * handler, or reused after resetting its state with Request::reuse().
 *
 * \context This function is \threadsafe. It may only be called when the camera
 * is in the Configured or Running state as defined in \ref camera_operation.
 *
 * \return A pointer to the newly created request, or nullptr on error
 */
std::unique_ptr<Request> Camera::createRequest(uint64_t cookie)

\brief Add a FrameBuffer with its associated Stream to the Request
 * \param[in] stream The stream the buffer belongs to
 * \param[in] buffer The FrameBuffer to add to the request
 * \param[in] fence The optional fence
 *
 * A reference to the buffer is stored in the request. The caller is responsible
 * for ensuring that the buffer will remain valid until the request complete
 * callback is called.
 *
 * A request can only contain one buffer per stream. If a buffer has already
 * been added to the request for the same stream, this function returns -EEXIST.
 *
 * A Fence can be optionally associated with the \a buffer.
 *
 * When a valid Fence is provided to this function, \a fence is moved to \a
 * buffer and this Request will only be queued to the device once the
 * fences of all its buffers have been correctly signalled. Ownership of the
 * fence will only be taken in case of success, otherwise the fence will
 * be left unmodified.
 *
 * If the \a fence associated with \a buffer isn't signalled, the request will
 * fail after a timeout. The buffer will still contain the fence, which
 * applications must retrieve with FrameBuffer::releaseFence() before the buffer
 * can be reused in another request. Attempting to add a buffer that still
 * contains a fence to a request will result in this function returning -EEXIST.
 *
 * \sa FrameBuffer::releaseFence()
 *
 * \return 0 on success or a negative error code otherwise
 * \retval -EEXIST The request already contains a buffer for the stream
 *  or the buffer still references a fence
 * \retval -EINVAL The buffer does not reference a valid Stream
 */
int Request::addBuffer(const Stream *stream, FrameBuffer *buffer,

\brief Retrieve the ID of the current thread
 *
 * The thread ID corresponds to the Linux thread ID (TID) as returned by the
 * gettid system call.
 *
 * \context This function is \threadsafe.
 *
 * \return The ID of the current thread
 */
pid_t Thread::currentId()
{
	ThreadData *data = ThreadData::current();
	return data->tid_;
}

findings.claim_quote: The caller must synchronize Camera::stop() with other functions that change the camera state, even when there are already submitted requests. \brief Create a request object for the camera
 * \param[in] cookie Opaque cookie for application use
 *
 * This function creates an empty request for the application to fill with
 * buffers and parameters, and queue for capture.
 *
 * The \a cookie is stored in the request and is accessible through the
 * Request::cookie() function at any time. It is typically used by applications
 * to map the request to an external resource in the request completion
 * handler, and is completely opaque to libcamera.
 *
 * The ownership of the returned request is passed to the caller, which is
 * responsible for deleting it. The request may be deleted in the completion
 * handler, or reused after resetting its state with Request::reuse().
 *
 * \context This function is \threadsafe. It may only be called when the camera
 * is in the Configured or Running state as defined in \ref camera_operation.
 *
 * \return A pointer to the newly created request, or nullptr on error
 */
std::unique_ptr<Request> Camera::createRequest(uint64_t cookie)

\brief Add a FrameBuffer with its associated Stream to the Request
 * \param[in] stream The stream the buffer belongs to
 * \param[in] buffer The FrameBuffer to add to the request
 * \param[in] fence The optional fence
 *
 * A reference to the buffer is stored in the request. The caller is responsible
 * for ensuring that the buffer will remain valid until the request complete
 * callback is called.
 *
 * A request can only contain one buffer per stream. If a buffer has already
 * been added to the request for the same stream, this function returns -EEXIST.
 *
 * A Fence can be optionally associated with the \a buffer.
 *
 * When a valid Fence is provided to this function, \a fence is moved to \a
 * buffer and this Request will only be queued to the device once the
 * fences of all its buffers have been correctly signalled. Ownership of the
 * fence will only be taken in case of success, otherwise the fence will
 * be left unmodified.
 *
 * If the \a fence associated with \a buffer isn't signalled, the request will
 * fail after a timeout. The buffer will still contain the fence, which
 * applications must retrieve with FrameBuffer::releaseFence() before the buffer
 * can be reused in another request. Attempting to add a buffer that still
 * contains a fence to a request will result in this function returning -EEXIST.
 *
 * \sa FrameBuffer::releaseFence()
 *
 * \return 0 on success or a negative error code otherwise
 * \retval -EEXIST The request already contains a buffer for the stream
 *  or the buffer still references a fence
 * \retval -EINVAL The buffer does not reference a valid Stream
 */
int Request::addBuffer(const Stream *stream, FrameBuffer *buffer,

 *

 * objects through the observer pattern without the need for boilerplate code.

 *

 * source. Slots are functions that are called in response to a signal. Signals
 * can be connected to and disconnected from slots dynamically at runtime. When
 * a signal is emitted, all connected slots are called sequentially in the order
 * they have been connected.
 *
 * Signals are defined with zero, one or more typed parameters. They are emitted

 * connected slots.
 *
 * Slots are normal static or class member functions. In order to be connected
 * to a signal, their signature must match the signal type (taking the same
 * arguments as the signal and returning void).
 *

 * arguments passed to the emit() function when the signal is emitted. Multiple
 * slots can be connected to the same signal, and multiple signals can connected
 * to the same slot.
 *

 *

findings.claim_quote: The caller of Camera::createRequest() receives ownership of the returned Request and is responsible for deleting it. The caller may delete the request in the completion handler or reuse it after resetting its state with Request::reuse(). Request::addBuffer() stores a reference to the buffer in the request, and the caller must ensure that the buffer remains valid until the request completion callback is called. The pipeline handler must not access the request after completeRequest() or cancelRequest() returns.

findings.claim_quote: completeBuffer emits bufferCompleted, then updates the request's internal buffer tracking and returns true if all buffers are complete or false if any buffers remain. The internal complete called by completeRequest selects RequestComplete if cancelled_ is false, or RequestCancelled if it is true.

\brief Add a FrameBuffer with its associated Stream to the Request
 * \param[in] stream The stream the buffer belongs to
 * \param[in] buffer The FrameBuffer to add to the request
 * \param[in] fence The optional fence
 *
 * A reference to the buffer is stored in the request. The caller is responsible
 * for ensuring that the buffer will remain valid until the request complete
 * callback is called.
 *
 * A request can only contain one buffer per stream. If a buffer has already
 * been added to the request for the same stream, this function returns -EEXIST.
 *
 * A Fence can be optionally associated with the \a buffer.
 *
 * When a valid Fence is provided to this function, \a fence is moved to \a
 * buffer and this Request will only be queued to the device once the
 * fences of all its buffers have been correctly signalled. Ownership of the
 * fence will only be taken in case of success, otherwise the fence will
 * be left unmodified.
 *
 * If the \a fence associated with \a buffer isn't signalled, the request will
 * fail after a timeout. The buffer will still contain the fence, which
 * applications must retrieve with FrameBuffer::releaseFence() before the buffer
 * can be reused in another request. Attempting to add a buffer that still
 * contains a fence to a request will result in this function returning -EEXIST.
 *
 * \sa FrameBuffer::releaseFence()
 *
 * \return 0 on success or a negative error code otherwise
 * \retval -EEXIST The request already contains a buffer for the stream
 *  or the buffer still references a fence
 * \retval -EINVAL The buffer does not reference a valid Stream
 */
int Request::addBuffer(const Stream *stream, FrameBuffer *buffer,

\brief Create a request object for the camera
 * \param[in] cookie Opaque cookie for application use
 *
 * This function creates an empty request for the application to fill with
 * buffers and parameters, and queue for capture.
 *
 * The \a cookie is stored in the request and is accessible through the
 * Request::cookie() function at any time. It is typically used by applications
 * to map the request to an external resource in the request completion
 * handler, and is completely opaque to libcamera.
 *
 * The ownership of the returned request is passed to the caller, which is
 * responsible for deleting it. The request may be deleted in the completion
 * handler, or reused after resetting its state with Request::reuse().
 *
 * \context This function is \threadsafe. It may only be called when the camera
 * is in the Configured or Running state as defined in \ref camera_operation.
 *
 * \return A pointer to the newly created request, or nullptr on error
 */
std::unique_ptr<Request> Camera::createRequest(uint64_t cookie)

\class Signal
 * \brief Generic signal and slot communication mechanism
 *
 * Signals and slots are a language construct aimed at communication between
 * objects through the observer pattern without the need for boilerplate code.
 * See http://doc.qt.io/qt-6/signalsandslots.html for more information.
 *
 * Signals model events that can be observed from objects unrelated to the event
 * source. Slots are functions that are called in response to a signal. Signals
 * can be connected to and disconnected from slots dynamically at runtime. When
 * a signal is emitted, all connected slots are called sequentially in the order
 * they have been connected.
 *
 * Signals are defined with zero, one or more typed parameters. They are emitted
 * with a value for each of the parameters, and those values are passed to the
 * connected slots.
 *
 * Slots are normal static or class member functions. In order to be connected
 * to a signal, their signature must match the signal type (taking the same
 * arguments as the signal and returning void).
 *
 * Connecting a signal to a slot results in the slot being called with the
 * arguments passed to the emit() function when the signal is emitted. Multiple
 * slots can be connected to the same signal, and multiple signals can connected
 * to the same slot.
 *
 * When a slot belongs to an instance of the Object class, the slot is called
 * in the context of the thread that the object is bound to. If the signal is
 * emitted from the same thread, the slot will be called synchronously, before
 * Signal::emit() returns. If the signal is emitted from a different thread,
 * the slot will be called asynchronously from the object's thread's event
 * loop, after the Signal::emit() function returns, with a copy of the signal's
 * arguments. The emitter shall thus ensure that any pointer or reference
 * passed through the signal will remain valid after the signal is emitted.
 *
 * Duplicate connections between a signal and a slot are not expected and use of
 * the Object class to manage signals will enforce this restriction.
 */

 * \fn Signal::connect

\class Signal
 * \brief Generic signal and slot communication mechanism
 *
 * Signals and slots are a language construct aimed at communication between
 * objects through the observer pattern without the need for boilerplate code.
 * See http://doc.qt.io/qt-6/signalsandslots.html for more information.
 *
 * Signals model events that can be observed from objects unrelated to the event
 * source. Slots are functions that are called in response to a signal. Signals
 * can be connected to and disconnected from slots dynamically at runtime. When
 * a signal is emitted, all connected slots are called sequentially in the order
 * they have been connected.
 *
 * Signals are defined with zero, one or more typed parameters. They are emitted
 * with a value for each of the parameters, and those values are passed to the
 * connected slots.
 *
 * Slots are normal static or class member functions. In order to be connected
 * to a signal, their signature must match the signal type (taking the same
 * arguments as the signal and returning void).
 *
 * Connecting a signal to a slot results in the slot being called with the
 * arguments passed to the emit() function when the signal is emitted. Multiple
 * slots can be connected to the same signal, and multiple signals can connected
 * to the same slot.
 *
 * When a slot belongs to an instance of the Object class, the slot is called
 * in the context of the thread that the object is bound to. If the signal is
 * emitted from the same thread, the slot will be called synchronously, before
 * Signal::emit() returns. If the signal is emitted from a different thread,
 * the slot will be called asynchronously from the object's thread's event
 * loop, after the Signal::emit() function returns, with a copy of the signal's
 * arguments. The emitter shall thus ensure that any pointer or reference
 * passed through the signal will remain valid after the signal is emitted.
 *
 * Duplicate connections between a signal and a slot are not expected and use of
 * the Object class to manage signals will enforce this restriction.
 */

findings.claim_quote: In the implementation, Signal::emit() calls activate for each slot and, when ConnectionTypeAuto detects different threads and selects ConnectionTypeQueued or when ConnectionTypeQueued is used explicitly, posts a message and returns without waiting. After Thread::postMessage() releases the queue lock, the receiving side's Thread::dispatchMessages() can call Object::message() and InvokeMessage::invoke(), so receiver execution on another thread can begin even before Signal::emit() returns; no general ordering around the return is guaranteed. Explicit ConnectionTypeDirect invokes the receiver immediately and synchronously on the sending thread, even if the receiving object belongs to another thread.

findings.condition: The proposed verification concerns delayed receivers, object lifetime, Direct reentry and Queued dispatch.
findings.actor: The sender and request owner coordinate lifetime; investigators record and check the specified events.
findings.timing: The plan tracks each delayed receiver's last use before deletion or reuse and distinguishes callback and stop boundaries.
findings.scope: A proposed investigation and conservative lifetime coordination, not an executed test or a claim that callbacks ran.
findings.reason: The plan is consistent with the pointer lifetime and connection contracts and checks the source's buffer-completion assertion. Its extra coordination is a plan, not a claim that the API assigns all coordination to the sender or automatically proves safe reuse. The English peer retains the plan and prohibition.

 *
 * An application needs to perform a sequence of operations on a camera before
 * it is ready to process requests. The camera needs to be acquired and
 * configured to prepare the camera for capture. Once started the camera can
 * process requests until it is stopped. When an application is done with a

/**
 * \page thread-safety Reentrancy and Thread-Safety
 *
 * Through the documentation, several terms are used to define how classes and
 * their member functions can be used from multiple threads.
 *
 * - A **reentrant** function may be called simultaneously from multiple
 *   threads if and only if each invocation uses a different instance of the
 *   class. This is the default for all member functions not explictly marked
 *   otherwise.
 *
 * - \anchor thread-safe A **thread-safe** function may be called
 *   simultaneously from multiple threads on the same instance of a class. A
 *   thread-safe function is thus reentrant. Thread-safe functions may also be
 *   called simultaneously with any other reentrant function of the same class
 *   on the same instance.
 *
 * \internal
 * - \anchor thread-bound A **thread-bound** function may be called only from
 *   the thread that the class instances lives in (see section \ref
 *   thread-objects). For instances of classes that do not derive from the
 *   Object class, this is the thread in which the instance was created. A
 *   thread-bound function is not thread-safe, and may or may not be reentrant.
 * \endinternal
 *
 * Neither reentrancy nor thread-safety, in this context, mean that a function
 * may be called simultaneously from the same thread, for instance from a
 * callback invoked by the function. This may deadlock and isn't allowed unless
 * separately documented.
 *
 * \if internal
 * A class is defined as reentrant, thread-safe or thread-bound if all its
 * member functions are reentrant, thread-safe or thread-bound respectively.
 * \else

 * are reentrant or thread-safe respectively.
 * \endif

\page thread Thread Support
 *
 * libcamera supports multi-threaded applications through a threading model that
 * sets precise rules to guarantee thread-safe usage of the API. Additionally,
 * libcamera makes internal use of threads, and offers APIs that simplify
 * interactions with application threads. Careful compliance with the threading
 * model will ensure avoidance of race conditions.
 *
 * Every thread created by libcamera is associated with an instance of the
 * Thread class. Those threads run an internal event loop by default to
 * dispatch events to objects. Additionally, the main thread of the application
 * (defined as the thread that calls CameraManager::start()) is also associated
 * with a Thread instance, but has no event loop accessible to libcamera. Other
 * application threads are not visible to libcamera.
 *
 * \section thread-objects Threads and Objects
 *
 * Instances of the Object class and all its derived classes are thread-aware
 * and are bound to the thread they are created in. They are said to *live* in
 * a thread, and they interact with the event loop of their thread for the
 * purpose of message passing and signal delivery. Messages posted to the
 * object with Object::postMessage() will be delivered from the event loop of
 * the thread that the object lives in. Signals delivered to the object, unless

\brief Add a FrameBuffer with its associated Stream to the Request
 * \param[in] stream The stream the buffer belongs to
 * \param[in] buffer The FrameBuffer to add to the request
 * \param[in] fence The optional fence
 *
 * A reference to the buffer is stored in the request. The caller is responsible
 * for ensuring that the buffer will remain valid until the request complete
 * callback is called.
 *
 * A request can only contain one buffer per stream. If a buffer has already
 * been added to the request for the same stream, this function returns -EEXIST.
 *
 * A Fence can be optionally associated with the \a buffer.
 *
 * When a valid Fence is provided to this function, \a fence is moved to \a
 * buffer and this Request will only be queued to the device once the
 * fences of all its buffers have been correctly signalled. Ownership of the
 * fence will only be taken in case of success, otherwise the fence will
 * be left unmodified.
 *
 * If the \a fence associated with \a buffer isn't signalled, the request will
 * fail after a timeout. The buffer will still contain the fence, which
 * applications must retrieve with FrameBuffer::releaseFence() before the buffer
 * can be reused in another request. Attempting to add a buffer that still
 * contains a fence to a request will result in this function returning -EEXIST.
 *
 * \sa FrameBuffer::releaseFence()
 *
 * \return 0 on success or a negative error code otherwise
 * \retval -EEXIST The request already contains a buffer for the stream
 *  or the buffer still references a fence
 * \retval -EINVAL The buffer does not reference a valid Stream
 */
int Request::addBuffer(const Stream *stream, FrameBuffer *buffer,

/**
 * \page thread-safety Reentrancy and Thread-Safety
 *
 * Through the documentation, several terms are used to define how classes and
 * their member functions can be used from multiple threads.
 *
 * - A **reentrant** function may be called simultaneously from multiple
 *   threads if and only if each invocation uses a different instance of the
 *   class. This is the default for all member functions not explictly marked
 *   otherwise.
 *
 * - \anchor thread-safe A **thread-safe** function may be called
 *   simultaneously from multiple threads on the same instance of a class. A
 *   thread-safe function is thus reentrant. Thread-safe functions may also be
 *   called simultaneously with any other reentrant function of the same class
 *   on the same instance.
 *
 * \internal
 * - \anchor thread-bound A **thread-bound** function may be called only from
 *   the thread that the class instances lives in (see section \ref
 *   thread-objects). For instances of classes that do not derive from the
 *   Object class, this is the thread in which the instance was created. A
 *   thread-bound function is not thread-safe, and may or may not be reentrant.
 * \endinternal
 *
 * Neither reentrancy nor thread-safety, in this context, mean that a function
 * may be called simultaneously from the same thread, for instance from a
 * callback invoked by the function. This may deadlock and isn't allowed unless
 * separately documented.
 *
 * \if internal
 * A class is defined as reentrant, thread-safe or thread-bound if all its
 * member functions are reentrant, thread-safe or thread-bound respectively.
 * \else
 * A class is defined as reentrant or thread-safe if all its member functions
 * are reentrant or thread-safe respectively.
 * \endif
 * Some member functions may additionally be documented as having additional
 * thread-related attributes.
 *
 * Most classes are reentrant but not thread-safe, as making them fully
 * thread-safe would incur locking costs considered prohibitive for the
 * expected use cases.
 */

\class Signal
 * \brief Generic signal and slot communication mechanism
 *
 * Signals and slots are a language construct aimed at communication between
 * objects through the observer pattern without the need for boilerplate code.
 * See http://doc.qt.io/qt-6/signalsandslots.html for more information.
 *
 * Signals model events that can be observed from objects unrelated to the event
 * source. Slots are functions that are called in response to a signal. Signals
 * can be connected to and disconnected from slots dynamically at runtime. When
 * a signal is emitted, all connected slots are called sequentially in the order
 * they have been connected.
 *
 * Signals are defined with zero, one or more typed parameters. They are emitted
 * with a value for each of the parameters, and those values are passed to the
 * connected slots.
 *
 * Slots are normal static or class member functions. In order to be connected
 * to a signal, their signature must match the signal type (taking the same
 * arguments as the signal and returning void).
 *
 * Connecting a signal to a slot results in the slot being called with the
 * arguments passed to the emit() function when the signal is emitted. Multiple
 * slots can be connected to the same signal, and multiple signals can connected
 * to the same slot.
 *
 * When a slot belongs to an instance of the Object class, the slot is called
 * in the context of the thread that the object is bound to. If the signal is
 * emitted from the same thread, the slot will be called synchronously, before
 * Signal::emit() returns. If the signal is emitted from a different thread,
 * the slot will be called asynchronously from the object's thread's event
 * loop, after the Signal::emit() function returns, with a copy of the signal's
 * arguments. The emitter shall thus ensure that any pointer or reference
 * passed through the signal will remain valid after the signal is emitted.
 *
 * Duplicate connections between a signal and a slot are not expected and use of
 * the Object class to manage signals will enforce this restriction.
 */

findings.claim_quote: The public virtual CPU probe was run three times. In each run, four requests were reported as RequestComplete, four as RequestCancelled, and there were 24 callbacks. There were 72 callbacks in total. In the public Virtual2 virtual probe on Ubuntu WSL2, Auto and Queued callbacks ran on the receiving object's main thread, while Direct callbacks ran on a different thread. Markers near callback entry and return for requests cancelled during stop were observed after stop-return for Auto and Queued, and between stop-enter and stop-return for Direct. The stop-enter and stop-return markers are application markers before and after the camera->stop() call, not exact instruction boundaries inside the function.

findings.condition: The observations use CPU-only memfd buffers and an unsignalled eventfd input in the specified Virtual2 probe.
findings.actor: The probe records actual application callbacks and retains the reported errors.
findings.timing: The near-return marker precedes the counter increment and local destruction; it does not trace completed C++ return.
findings.scope: Controlled virtual-probe evidence; DMA synchronization, physical capture, other applications and the internal HAL remain unvalidated.
findings.reason: The Korean and English claims preserve the marker limitation, observed callback scope and exclusions in the evidence. They do not turn the probe into physical-device verification.

sources.source_quote:
\brief Add a FrameBuffer with its associated Stream to the Request
 * \param[in] stream The stream the buffer belongs to
 * \param[in] buffer The FrameBuffer to add to the request
 * \param[in] fence The optional fence
 *
 * A reference to the buffer is stored in the request. The caller is responsible
 * for ensuring that the buffer will remain valid until the request complete
 * callback is called.
 *
 * A request can only contain one buffer per stream. If a buffer has already
 * been added to the request for the same stream, this function returns -EEXIST.
 *
 * A Fence can be optionally associated with the \a buffer.
 *
 * When a valid Fence is provided to this function, \a fence is moved to \a
 * buffer and this Request will only be queued to the device once the
 * fences of all its buffers have been correctly signalled. Ownership of the
 * fence will only be taken in case of success, otherwise the fence will
 * be left unmodified.
 *
 * If the \a fence associated with \a buffer isn't signalled, the request will
 * fail after a timeout. The buffer will still contain the fence, which
 * applications must retrieve with FrameBuffer::releaseFence() before the buffer
 * can be reused in another request. Attempting to add a buffer that still
 * contains a fence to a request will result in this function returning -EEXIST.
 *
 * \sa FrameBuffer::releaseFence()
 *
 * \return 0 on success or a negative error code otherwise
 * \retval -EEXIST The request already contains a buffer for the stream
 *  or the buffer still references a fence
 * \retval -EINVAL The buffer does not reference a valid Stream
 */
int Request::addBuffer(const Stream *stream, FrameBuffer *buffer,

findings.claim_quote: Request::addBuffer는 버퍼에 대한 참조를 요청에 저장합니다. 호출자는 요청 완료 콜백이 호출될 때까지 해당 버퍼가 유효하게 남아 있도록 보장해야 합니다. Request::addBuffer가 성공하면 유효한 Fence의 소유권은 buffer(FrameBuffer)로 이동합니다. 이때 fence는 buffer로 옮겨집니다.

findings.claim_quote: Request::addBuffer stores a reference to the buffer in the request. The caller must ensure that the buffer remains valid until the request completion callback is invoked. If Request::addBuffer succeeds, ownership of the valid Fence moves to buffer (FrameBuffer). At that point, fence is moved to buffer.

findings.condition: Registration occurs when a request is created; the queue operations describe the named pipeline handler method.
findings.actor: PipelineHandler registers the prepared callback and queues the request in the associated camera's private data.
findings.timing: The prepared callback calls doQueueRequests when invoked; queueRequest pushes the request before calling prepare with 300 ms.
findings.scope: Registration and preparation dispatch; the 300 ms argument is not a capture or completion guarantee.
findings.reason: The sources identify the callback's invoked function and the same camera-owned waiting queue and request preparation call. The related peers describe compatible dispatch and thread context.
findings.claim_quote: PipelineHandler::registerRequest()는 요청이 생성될 때 호출됩니다. 이 시점에 pipeline handler가 해당 요청에 필요한 일회성 초기화를 수행할 수 있습니다. PipelineHandler::registerRequest()에서 request->_d()->prepared 신호에 연결된 람다 콜백이 실제로 호출하는 함수는 doQueueRequests입니다. PipelineHandler::queueRequest는 요청이 가리키는 카메라의 내부 waitingRequests_ 큐에 요청을 추가한 뒤, 같은 요청의 prepare 호출에 300ms 시간 인자를 전달합니다.

findings.reason: 람다의 호출 대상과 카메라별 대기 큐, 준비 대상 요청이 소스와 일치합니다. 관련 피어도 준비와 대기 큐 등록을 구분합니다.
findings.claim_quote: PipelineHandler::registerRequest() is called when a request is created. At this point, the pipeline handler may perform the one-time initialization that the request requires. In PipelineHandler::registerRequest(), the function that the lambda callback connected to the request->_d()->prepared signal actually calls is doQueueRequests. PipelineHandler::queueRequest adds the request to the internal waitingRequests_ queue of the camera that the request refers to, and then passes a 300ms time argument to the prepare call on the same request.

findings.reason: 영문은 한국어의 조건과 취소 및 통지 의미를 보존하며, 소스의 준비 흐름과 일치합니다.
findings.claim_quote: Request::Private::prepare creates and connects EventNotifier, which waits for the fd to become readable, for each acquire fence of each FrameBuffer in pending_, and notifierActivated is called when a fence is signalled. If there are no fences to wait on, notifiers_ is empty, so the Request::prepared signal is emitted immediately and the return happens right away. Only when the optional timeout argument is not 0 ms and there are fences to wait on is Timer created and started with the timeout duration; if not all fences have been correctly signalled when the timeout expires, Request is cancelled and the Request::prepared signal is emitted. This timer is created when prepare is called, not in the Request constructor, so that it is bound to the pipeline handler thread.

\brief Complete a buffer for a request
 * \param[in] request The request the buffer belongs to
 * \param[in] buffer The buffer that has completed
 *
 * This function shall be called by pipeline handlers to signal completion of
 * the \a buffer part of the \a request. It notifies applications of buffer
 * completion and updates the request's internal buffer tracking. The request
 * is not completed automatically when the last buffer completes to give
 * pipeline handlers a chance to perform any operation that may still be
 * needed. They shall complete requests explicitly with completeRequest().
 *
 * \context This function shall be called from the CameraManager thread.
 *
 * \return True if all buffers contained in the request have completed, false
 * otherwise
 */
bool PipelineHandler::completeBuffer(Request *request, FrameBuffer *buffer)
{
	Camera *camera = request->_d()->camera();
	camera->bufferCompleted.emit(request, buffer);
	return request->_d()->completeBuffer(buffer);
}

camera-model.md/concurrency/2.text: `Camera::start`의 context 주석은 호출자가 카메라 상태에 영향을 주는 다른 함수와 동기화해야 한다고 명시합니다. `Camera::stop`의 context 주석도 같은 범위의 동기화 의무를 호출자에게 명시합니다. 따라서 호출자는 `start`와 `stop` 호출을 카메라 상태에 영향을 주는 다른 함수들과 동기화해야 합니다.

camera-model.md/concurrency/3.text: `completeRequest()`를 호출하는 파이프라인 핸들러는 `CameraManager` 스레드에서 호출해야 합니다. 이 함수의 `\context` 항목은 호출 스레드를 `CameraManager` 스레드로 명시하며, 이는 호출하는 쪽이 지켜야 하는 조건입니다. 이 주석은 애플리케이션 콜백이 실행되는 스레드를 명시하지 않습니다.
